15.2.5T4 | Exit, Transfer, and Preservation of Evolutionary Memory ​

In briefT4 makes safe exit and uptake verifiable while preserving responsibility and minimum necessary memory; exit does not mean deleting an object or forcing someone to stay.
Codes used in this section (2)
  • T0Carriers of Safety and Trust
  • C12Check on the Validity of Normative Bridging

T4 applies when staying or repairing is no longer safe, feasible, or justified. T4 can be assessed directly as a candidate without any prior T level if T0 cannot be established, anti-retaliation and appeal repeatedly fail, repair is blocked by power, the object’s anchor has effectively been lost, the net harm of staying exceeds the cost of transfer, or outside arrangements for taking over are safer. Actual exit, transfer, or handling of memory still requires normative choice, C12, J, and O1–O4.

Permitted actions include designing safe exit, local buffers, staged transfer, and alternative arrangements to take over. Preserve evidence, skills, lessons from failure, and attempts at repair only with consent and to the minimum extent necessary. Settle care, compensation, and outstanding responsibilities. Protect those who stay and those unable to exit. Verify the new system taking over and retain an option for a second transfer. A costly strategic action can be considered only if the subject participates voluntarily and with knowledge, can bear the cost, explicitly records the experience, and does not exhaust all their remaining strength.

Do not romanticize exit as courageous, loyal, mature, or the only right course. Do not help responsible parties use exit to evade compensation, care, or legal duties. Do not require people affected to publicly prove their circumstances. Individual material must not be entered into public memory without consent. Do not assume the new system is inherently safe. Do not conscript others’ love and sacrifice.

For people unable to exit, the goal is to reduce harm, preserve subjecthood, restore minimal choices, and establish local buffers and a future way out. It is not to “complete an ideal exit.” The wish to leave, hesitation, wariness about the new carrier, and anomalies among those who stay are weak signals. T4 must not become a unilateral escape for those with more resources. If exiting, refusing a transfer, preserving evidence, or appealing is followed by withdrawal of supplies, tracking, stigma, or retaliation against those who stay, review protection and halt the steps that increase danger.

Suspend or redirect the affected steps of transfer, contact, or data handling when risks in the new arrangements increase, the subject withdraws, exit provokes retaliation, memory is used beyond the permitted purpose, obligations are evaded, or authorization ceases to hold. Suspension does not require a subject to remain exposed to danger. Continue necessary support on independently valid grounds. Restore rights and resources that can be restored, revoke data uses outside the permitted scope, correct/delete records, and remedy harm to the subject and to those who stay. On entry to the new system, register T0, scale, and K for the new object. Do not carry over the old authorization.

Exit involves more than deleting an object from a table. Ending an organization, changing jobs, separating within a family, relocating, and retiring a tool can leave responsibilities for wages, care, debts, compensation, knowledge handover, and data custody. Obtain separate evidence that the new arrangements actually operate, dependents receive support, those who leave are protected against retaliation, and historical responsibilities have been handled. The name of an alternative or a handover document cannot substitute for this evidence. 〔Studies 16.08–16.09, 23.04, 24.06, 28.08, 29.08〕

Assessing success or failure in T0–T4 first requires fixing the function and conditions of support at issue. The ability to express oneself with continuing assistance, availability of a service with a temporary power supply, or continuation of a task by replacement staff can all be accurately limited outcomes. If the goal includes independent completion, stability over the whole period, or full recovery of living conditions, check separately what happens after support is withdrawn, what resources are available afterward, and whether the relevant endpoints are reached. An uncompleted broader goal does not cancel a narrower one already achieved. Achieving the narrower goal does not establish full recovery.

When work is taken over after an exit, distinguish who carries out tasks, who arranges and verifies them, who is on call, and who bears the costs. If the person previously responsible still arranges and checks tasks after handover, acknowledge the reduction in execution work and retain the coordination burden that has not been transferred. Safe exit does not require affected people to supply a perfect replacement first. Where bounded responsibilities still have independent grounds, parties with authority and resources must state the scope and duration of the arrangements for taking over and the gaps that remain. The need for continuity must not be rewritten as a requirement that the original party stay indefinitely.

15.2.5Note

Understanding this section

15.2.5 T4 | Exit, Transfer, and Preservation of Evolutionary Memory

T4 makes safe exit and uptake verifiable while preserving responsibility and minimum necessary memory; exit does not mean deleting an object or forcing someone to stay.

Short quotation translated from Chinese: “Exit does not mean deleting the object from a table.” Exit may be assessed when continued residence or repair is unsafe, infeasible, or unjustified. T0 being impossible to establish, persistent failure of protection against retaliation and appeals, repair blocked by power, substantive loss of an anchor, net harm from staying exceeding transfer costs, or safer external uptake may all directly make T4 a candidate. “Candidate” is not permission to execute: normative choice, C12, J, and O1–O4 still apply in full. [T-4; T-main]

Permitted measures include safe exit, local buffering, phased transfer, and alternative uptake; consensual preservation of evidence, skills, lessons from failure, and repair attempts limited to what is necessary; settlement of care, compensation, and unfulfilled responsibilities; protection of those staying and those unable to exit; verification of new uptake; and retention of a second transfer option. Strategic actions involving costs may become candidates only when the person voluntarily gives informed consent, costs are bearable, experience is explicitly recorded, and remaining strength is not exhausted. Others’ sacrifices cannot be requisitioned. [T-4]

Exit is neither an identity test of courage, loyalty, or maturity nor the only correct choice. It must not help responsible parties evade compensation, care, or legal duties; require affected people to prove their experiences publicly; turn personal material into public memory without consent; or presume that a new system is inherently safe. Preserving experience and disseminating it publicly involve different objects, uses, and permissions. [T-4]

For people unable to exit, the goals are harm reduction, agency, minimum choice, local buffers, and future exits; an ideal completed exit is not required. Hesitation, wariness of a new carrier, the desire to exit, and anomalies among those staying are all weak signals. When those with more resources leave the remaining costs to others, completing the transfer does not make it justified. Withdrawal of supplies, tracking, stigmatization, or retaliation against those staying must trigger protection review and stop the steps that increase risk. [T-4]

When risks in new uptake rise, the subject withdraws, exit triggers retaliation, memory exceeds its permitted use, obligations are evaded, or authorization becomes invalid, suspend or reroute the relevant transfer, contact, or data processing. Suspension must not require the person to remain dangerously exposed. Necessary support with an independently valid basis should continue, alongside restoration of recoverable rights and resources, revocation of out-of-scope uses, correction or deletion of records, and remedies for harm to the person and those staying. These measures also need independent grounds; protection must not become a pretext for expanding one’s own power. [T-4; T-state]

Entry into a new system requires re-registration using the new object’s T0, scale, and K; old authorization does not automatically travel with people or data. Organizational closure, job changes, family separation, relocation, and tool retirement may each leave responsibilities for wages, care, debts, compensation, knowledge transfer, or data custody. Actual operation of new arrangements, support for dependents, absence of retaliation against those exiting, and handling of historical responsibilities each require evidence. A signature on a handover form cannot establish all of them. [T-4]

This section also clarifies outcome endpoints for all T types: being able to express oneself with continuing assistance, having a service available through temporary power, and replacement personnel carrying on work are all narrow outcomes that may hold under explicit support conditions. Independent performance, stability throughout the entire period, and full restoration of life require separate examination of withdrawal of assistance, subsequent resources, and the corresponding endpoints. Full recovery being incomplete must not negate narrow outcomes; nor may narrow outcomes be advertised as full recovery. [T-4]

Exit continuity requires separate examination of execution, arrangement and verification, standby, and payment. If the original responsible person still arranges and checks work after handing over its execution, reduced execution work can be recognized while recording the remaining coordination burden. Safe exit does not require the person to provide a perfect replacement first. For limited responsibilities with continuing independent grounds, actors with the necessary authority and resources must specify scope, duration, and gaps; these must not be rewritten as an unlimited duty to stay. [T-4; T-care]

GOV.UK’s service-retirement guidance separately requires consideration of needs after retirement, notification of nondigital and assisted users, and protection of data. This indicates that responsibilities after retirement do not disappear when the service is switched off. Guidance for institutional services cannot provide grounds for requiring an individual to continue dangerous contact, however. Only uptake of needs and data responsibilities are compared here; no particular retirement outcome is evaluated. [P-RETIRE]

How the argument develops

  1. 1

    Compare the risks of staying and transferring, treating exit as a candidate rather than an identity command.

  2. 2

    Determine limited actions according to the person’s choice, norms, and authority.

  3. 3

    Arrange new uptake, support for those staying, outstanding responsibilities, and minimum necessary memory separately.

  4. 4

    Monitor risks and withdrawal at each step; if risks increase, suspend or reroute rather than force someone to remain in danger.

  5. 5

    Reestablish conditions for the new object; recognize narrow outcomes according to support and endpoints, and distinguish execution burdens from coordination burdens.

Distinctions to keep clear

Safe exit

Protect the person’s choice and lawfully continue limited responsibilities.

≠

Unlimited duty to stay

A perfect replacement cannot be made a prerequisite for exit.

Memory preservation

Consent, minimum necessity, and limited use.

≠

Appropriation for public narratives

Personal material must not be disclosed without consent.

Transfer of execution

Others carry out the work.

≠

Transfer of coordination

Arrangements, verification, standby, and payment require separate checks.

Success with support

Actually holds under explicit conditions.

≠

Comprehensive recovery

Requires a broader endpoint and subsequent evidence.

Teaching construction: execution decreases while coordination remainsTeaching scenario

AssumptionsObjects, values, and events are teaching stipulations.

A constructed care arrangement originally involves 4 hours of daily care work and 1 hour of coordination. A replacement takes over all 4 hours of care work, while the original provider still coordinates for 1 hour. The original provider’s daily care work has decreased by 4 hours; their burden has not fallen to zero. If coordination constitutes an independently established bounded responsibility, specify its period and uptake gaps. The remaining hour does not negate the 4-hour reduction, nor justify requiring indefinite continued service.

BoundaryAn artificial construction testing responsibilities and boundaries only, not actual intervention effects.

Teaching construction: service with auxiliary powerTeaching scenario

AssumptionsObjects, values, and events are teaching stipulations.

Suppose a constructed backup supply supports 6 hours, during which critical services are observed to remain available. The functional outcome for that window may hold; if the target is 24-hour continuity or stability after backup is withdrawn, evidence is still missing for 18 hours and the conditions of withdrawal. Six hours of success is neither no outcome nor completion of 24 hours.

BoundaryAn artificial construction testing responsibilities and boundaries only, not actual intervention effects.

Responsibilities for users and data remain after service retirementDocumented case

GOV.UK’s service-retirement guidance, published in 2016 and updated in 2025 on the page read for this guide, requires consideration of subsequent user needs, notification of nondigital and assisted users, and arrangements for data protection.

SourceGOV.UK Service Manual：Retiring your service‘Consider user needs’; ‘Telling your users’; ‘Protecting information’ (webpage lines 72—165)Reading scope: Partly read

Scope and limitsThe institutional text is used only to explain that retirement does not mean responsibilities disappear. It is not a specific retirement outcome, and it cannot be extrapolated into a requirement that an individual remain dangerously exposed.

Scope and open questions

Source rules and bounded real-world materials remain separate; cases illustrate only local mechanisms and do not certify entire-framework compliance.

It may enter candidate assessment directly, without omitting normative choice, protection, or valid authorization.

If a transfer is suspended, must the person return to danger?

No; pause the relevant risk-increasing links and separately continue independently valid support.

Basis: T4 stopping paragraph.

Must the original responsible person find a perfect replacement before exiting?

Safe exit is not conditional on this; those with authority and resources must specify the scope, period, and gaps of bounded responsibilities.

Basis: T4 final paragraph.

Does functioning only with assistance mean there is no outcome?

The narrow outcome under those support conditions may be acknowledged; broader goals require separate checking.

Basis: T4 outcome-endpoint paragraph.

15.3Common Checks for the Application Modules ​

In briefModules change questions and risk checks, not replace objects, facts, or authority; gaps propagate proposition by proposition, while independently established judgments remain.
Codes used in this section (1)
  • D0Structural Object

A domain name does not supply an object contract. For each application, first register the D0 object, nine-axis scale SP=<A,X,T,O,C,R,I,N,J>, K, time window, sources, and affected and low-power positions. Then enter the seven-gate tool workflow. An application module can change only the questions asked, risk checks, and action ceiling. It cannot substitute for domain investigation, professional judgment, legal procedures, or authorization.

All nine modules retain PF-1 through PF-10. They register affected and low-power positions, provide anonymous submission, submission through a representative, and low-exposure submission, and preserve refusal and stopping. They also require effective appeal, anti-retaliation, evidence supplementation and record correction, and external independent review. The remaining requirements are withdrawal, rollback, repair and version write-back, exit and transfer with protection through representatives when exit is impossible, and the action ceiling, prohibited actions, and stop triggers.

Each module below specifies the scope of domain evidence and how to downgrade outputs for gaps. It states what judgments the available materials can support, what facts and verification are still missing, and how those gaps limit the output. Each supported proposition has its own claim_id, material references in source_refs, and a value for max_inference from the closed set. A module title or list of materials cannot support a whole passage of conclusions.

Partial coverage can still be useful. The output ceiling must fall in line with the gaps. Every source_gap_effects entry must select from the closed enumerations “lower confidence, suspend the proposition, require external verification, or record only a gap in the inventory” and “no external action, require a domain protocol, narrow authorization, or suspend intervention.” It must not be none or ignore. The effects of gaps propagate along the dependencies of each proposition. A gap in one item does not invalidate all analysis. Argument evaluations, procedural critiques, and conditional recommendations under explicit premises can be retained separately when they have independent grounds.

15.3Note

Understanding this section

15.3 Common checks for application modules

Modules change questions and risk checks, not replace objects, facts, or authority; gaps propagate proposition by proposition, while independently established judgments remain.

Short quotation translated from Chinese: “A domain name is not an object contract.” Saying “family,” “platform,” or “emergency” identifies only an entry point; it cannot omit the D0 object, nine-axis SP=<A,X,T,O,C,R,I,N,J>, K, time window, sources, or affected/low-power positions. A family may involve both care chains and property eligibility; a platform may involve a fixed interface or a model in training. Different objects entail different evidence and authority. [T-main]

After registration, enter the seven-gate tool process. Modules adjust what to ask, which risks to check, and where outputs stop; they cannot replace domain investigation, professional judgment, legal procedures, or authorization. A larger sphere of influence I does not generate J-axis authority. Using general advice to revoke eligibility changes the actual use and requires renewed checking of strong-judgment and disposition procedures. [T-main；T-tools；T-strong；T-scale]

All nine modules retain all ten PF protections: affected and low-power positions; anonymity, proxies, and low exposure; refusal and stopping; effective appeals; protection against retaliation; supplementary evidence and correction; external independent review; withdrawal, rollback, repair, and version write-back; exit, transfer, and proxy protection for those unable to exit; and action ceilings, prohibited actions, and stopping triggers. One cannot select only anonymity or logging because they are easier to implement technically. [T-main；T-protection]

Every supported proposition should have an independent claim_id, source_refs, and closed max_inference: a material is responsible only for the corresponding object, window, and inference ceiling. The appearance of a platform paper in a materials catalog does not endorse an entire passage’s conclusions about fairness, safety, user psychology, and expanded governance. This text expresses the same responsibility through paragraph-level source IDs and an accurate source table, but teaching examples are not valid execution records of an engineering contract. [T-main]

The original limits missingness effects to two closed sets: on the knowledge side, “lower confidence, defer the proposition, require external verification, or only register a catalog gap”; on the action side, “no external action, require a domain protocol, narrow authorization, or defer intervention.” source_gap_effects cannot be none or ignore. Choose according to specific dependencies; do not generically record every gap as lowering confidence while retaining the original action authority. [T-main]

Partial coverage is not useless. Without field data, facts or effects dependent on the field cannot be established; independently grounded textual evaluation, procedural criticism, and conditional recommendations with explicit premises may still hold. Conversely, the actual presence of an appeal entry in a text does not prove accessibility in practice. Evidence for another proposition cannot fill this gap. [T-main]

The common checks specify research responsibilities only; they do not independently demonstrate any domain intervention’s effectiveness, so this unit uses teaching examples of proposition dependencies. The following nine modules separately register objects, weak signals, low-power positions, inability to exit, protection against retaliation, prohibited actions, stopping, and downgrades for missing evidence. This general rule cannot replace elaboration within each domain. [T-main]

How the argument develops

  1. 1

    First rewrite domain labels as objects, scales, K, and windows.

  2. 2

    Register supported propositions, their materials, and inference ceilings individually.

  3. 3

    Check all ten PF items and the actual purpose of use.

  4. 4

    Propagate gaps along dependencies, specifying consequences on the knowledge and action sides.

  5. 5

    Retain independently established criticism and recommendations; do not let local blanks contaminate every judgment.

Distinctions to keep clear

Domain entry point

Identifies risks to check.

≠

Object contract

Fixes this inquiry’s object and evidential responsibility.

Catalog coverage

A relevant material entry exists.

≠

Proposition support

The material actually supports the specified inference.

Partial coverage

Downgrade affected propositions.

≠

Everything invalid

One cannot reject the whole without dependency analysis.

Teaching construction: downgrading two propositions separatelyTeaching scenario

AssumptionsEntirely constructed scenarios and values, used to test inference ceilings.

A fictional platform’s public rules say “appeals are available,” so proposition A, “the text lists an entry point,” has textual support. Proposition B, “all users can actually appeal,” lacks testing and group-specific records. Retain A; defer B and require external verification. Do not deny A because B has a gap, or use A to permit expanded bans.

BoundaryNot evidence from a real investigation, professional diagnosis, or effects of intervention.

What counterexamples change

Teaching counterexampleTeaching counterexample: claiming a platform is fair merely because a platform paper is listed makes a materials catalog endorse an entire passage.

What it limitsLimits unconditional extension of this section without negating independently grounded bounded judgments.

Historical research manuscript: Xikari, On Conditions, Structure, and Transformation

Sourced counterexampleBoundary in the original: complete fields grant no access, disposition authority, or professional qualification.

What it limitsLimits unconditional extension of this section without negating independently grounded bounded judgments.

Historical research manuscript: Xikari, On Conditions, Structure, and Transformation

Sourced counterexampleBoundary in the original: local missingness does not automatically delete independently grounded procedural criticism.

What it limitsLimits unconditional extension of this section without negating independently grounded bounded judgments.

Historical research manuscript: Xikari, On Conditions, Structure, and Transformation

What does not follow

  • Teaching counterexample: claiming a platform is fair merely because a platform paper is listed makes a materials catalog endorse an entire passage.
  • Boundary in the original: complete fields grant no access, disposition authority, or professional qualification.
  • Boundary in the original: local missingness does not automatically delete independently grounded procedural criticism.

Scope and open questions

The common checks are methodological and normative conditions, illustrated with reviewable teaching constructions; no actual implementation effects are invented.

  • This lesson undertakes no execution in a real setting; professional protocols, field facts, valid authorization, and protective effects require separate verification.
  • External evidence supports only the propositions listed in the source table; material titles do not fill unread portions or unmeasured effects.

  3. 3

    Can a module name determine authority?

Without field records, is even textual criticism prohibited?

Independently grounded textual criticism may remain; factual and action dependencies require separate checks.

Basis: Gap propagation under the common checks.

What is wrong with entering only none to indicate no materials?

It bypasses closed registration of missingness effects and does not specify which inferences or actions are restricted.

Basis: The source_gap_effects rule.

Can a module name determine authority?

No; a specific object and valid authorization are required.

Basis: Opening paragraph of the common checks.

15.3.1APP-REL | Relationships ​

In briefRelationship analysis concerns concrete interactions and commitments; where coercion or inability to exit freely appears, stop joint diagnosis and turn to safety support.
Codes used in this section (2)
  • T0Carriers of Safety and Trust
  • T4Exit, Transfer, and Preservation of Evolutionary Memory

The object is the interaction, shared commitments, boundaries, division of responsibility, and return flows within a particular time window. It does not encompass either party’s personality. A relationship, an individual’s psychology, family institutions, and events involving violence or coercion are distinct objects. Register scale and K again when the object changes.

Major risks include romanticizing one-sided effort as love, assuming both parties want repair, exposing people again through forced dialogue, underestimating dependence and the cost of exit, and weaponizing the framework’s terms. A lightweight entry asks first about felt safety, whether responsibility runs only one way, whether effort is reciprocated, whether both parties want to work toward repair, and whether boundaries can be respected. In the presence of violence, coercion, sustained humiliation, control of resources, isolation, continuing deception, or inability to exit freely, stop the joint diagnosis and turn to safety and external support.

Weak signals include hesitation, silence, avoidance, informal requests for help, and repeated boundary crossings. Register low-power positions in terms of dependence on housing, resources, care, identity, and reputation. People unable to exit may submit through a representative, disclose in stages, and use local buffers. Threats and changes in resources after setting a boundary, seeking help, refusing dialogue, or expressing a wish to leave enter anti-retaliation monitoring.

The tool can produce at most plain-language observations, escalation of risk, needs for external support, and candidates for T0–T4. It authorizes no mediation, disclosure, separation, or disposition of property. It does not diagnose personality or illness or substitute for psychological, medical, or legal judgment.

Scope of domain evidence and downgrading for gaps (partial coverage). The framework’s rules support a lightweight entry into relationship analysis, protection in informal settings, and protection for people unable to exit. Independent causal contracts for relationships, systematic cases, and evidence of intervention effects are still missing. The output can therefore include only observations, escalation of risk, and needs for support. It cannot determine personality, causal responsibility, or the effectiveness of intervention on that basis. Where violence, coercion, or consequences for property, residence, or guardianship are involved, hand the matter to the appropriate professional procedure and narrow the action ceiling.

15.3.1Note

Understanding this section

15.3.1 APP-REL | Relationships

Relationship analysis concerns concrete interactions and commitments; where coercion or inability to exit freely appears, stop joint diagnosis and turn to safety support.

Short quotation translated from Chinese: “not either party’s personality.” The object is interactions, shared commitments, boundaries, burden sharing, and returns within a particular window. A relationship dyad, individual psychology, family institutions, and incidents of violence/coercion cannot be conflated. Any conversion requires registering scale and K anew; descriptions of interaction cannot be upgraded into personality or disease diagnoses. [T-1]

The lightweight entry first asks about felt safety, whether responsibility is one-sided, whether contributions receive returns, whether both parties are willing to repair the relationship jointly, and whether boundaries can be respected. These are observational questions, not inputs to an overall relationship score. Love, longevity, or responsibility cannot turn unilateral depletion into a normative obligation. Willingness for joint repair must be checked separately for each party; one person’s requesting counseling does not imply both are willing. [T-1]

Where there is violence, coercion, prolonged humiliation, resource control, isolation, persistent deception, or inability to exit freely, stop joint diagnosis and turn to safety and external support. What stops is the joint procedure that would increase exposure, not acknowledgment of the person’s request for help. Nor does the framework independently order separation, disclosure, or disposal of property. [T-1]

Hesitation, silence, avoidance, informal help-seeking, and repeated boundary violations can all be registered as weak signals, without directly determining personality or motives. List low-power positions separately through dependencies involving housing, resources, care, status, and reputation. Those unable to exit may use proxies, phased disclosure, and local buffers. Threats or resource changes after setting boundaries, seeking help, refusing dialogue, or exiting require protective review and monitoring against retaliation. [T-1]

Outputs are limited to natural-language observations, risk escalation, needs for external support, and candidate T types. The module authorizes neither mediation, disclosure, separation, nor property disposition; it does not diagnose disease or replace psychological, medical, or legal judgment. A candidate T4 cannot become an order that the person leave immediately. Real paths, choices, professional procedures, and authority require separate checking. [T-1；T-types]

Coverage in this domain is partial: framework protection rules exist, but independent relationship-causation contracts, systematic cases, and evidence of intervention effects are missing. Thus one cannot claim to have proved who caused relationship failure, who has a personality defect, or that an intervention works. Consequences involving violence, property, residence, or custody require corresponding professional procedures and narrowed action ceilings; referral is not completed professional judgment. [T-1]

The publication page for WHO’s 2014 handbook distinguishes immediate emotional and physical needs, ongoing safety, and further support, and explicitly says the basic guidelines do not directly address people under 18 or men. This shows that domain support itself has an object and scope. Only the official introduction was read here; the PDF was not obtained. It is not presented as complete clinical grounds, nor are situations of violence rewritten as ordinary communication conflicts. [P-WHO]

How the argument develops

  1. 1

    Fix the object as interaction; do not personalize it into a personality judgment.

  2. 2

    First check safety, one-sided responsibility, and genuine willingness for repair.

  3. 3

    Protect hesitation and dependent positions; do not compel disclosure.

  4. 4

    Stop joint diagnosis and move to safety support where coercion or restricted exit exists.

  5. 5

    With partial evidence, output only observations and support needs; handle professional consequences separately.

Distinctions to keep clear

Observation of interaction

Behavior within a particular relationship window.

≠

Personality diagnosis

Requires independent professional evidence, which this module does not provide.

Joint repair

Every party is genuinely willing and safe.

≠

One party’s commitment

Cannot represent the other party.

Support for help-seeking

Provides optional safe entry points.

≠

Forced departure

The framework has no authority to decide for the person.

Teaching construction: two refusals and an erroneous labelTeaching scenario

AssumptionsEntirely constructed scenarios and values, used to test inference ceilings.

Fictional A refuses joint meetings twice, explaining that B controls housing and resources. The refusals and dependency may be recorded, and whether meetings increase risk checked. The number of refusals cannot become an “immature” label, nor determine all disputed facts by itself.

BoundaryNot evidence from a real investigation, professional diagnosis, or effects of intervention.

Objects and types of needs in WHO’s 2014 clinical handbookDocumented case

Scope and open questions

Cases serve local factual or institutional comparisons; theoretical rules, original evidence, teaching constructions, and unresolved authority are labeled separately.

  • External evidence supports only the propositions listed in the source table; material titles do not fill unread portions or unmeasured effects.

May refusal to attend a meeting be recorded as insincerity about repair?

No automatic inference is allowed; refusal itself is protected. Check safety and dependency first.

Basis: REL weak signals and prohibitive boundaries.

May the framework justify recommending disposal of the other person’s property?

No; property consequences require corresponding legal procedures and valid authority.

Basis: REL action ceiling.

Without causal evidence, may safety needs be identified?

With proportionate indications, risks and needs for external support may be recorded without claiming to assign responsibility.

Basis: REL downgrades for missing evidence.

15.3.2APP-FAM | Families ​

In briefFamily boundaries require separate checks for the rights, resources, and care at issue; co-residence or “the whole family’s interests” cannot substitute for members’ consent.
Codes used in this section (2)
  • T0Carriers of Safety and Trust
  • T4Exit, Transfer, and Preservation of Evolutionary Memory

The family module checks co-residence, recognition of kinship, affection, property, care, labor, and legal eligibility separately. It assumes no membership boundary that assigns all rights and duties at once. People who live together need not jointly control resources. People who provide care need not acquire inheritance rights. Legally recognized family members may live apart for long periods. The nuclear family can be a particular statistical category and must not be assumed to be the only real form or the normative standard. A family as a whole, a relationship between two people, a chain of care, an individual safety event, and an external institution are distinct objects. Birth, death, illness, migration, and changes in guardianship or economic dependence may require rechecking the corresponding boundaries and K.

Major risks include recording children and dependents as consenting when they cannot exit, low visibility of care work and health costs, treating control of resources and isolation as private matters, overriding individual rights in the name of the family as a whole, and conscripting love, filial duty, responsibility, and sacrifice. Children, older people, patients, people with disabilities, economically dependent people, and primary caregivers must be listed separately.

Weak signals may be expressed in behavior, indirectly, through a representative, or after a delay. Members with little power must not bear the costs of maintaining the appearance of family stability. When people cannot leave, provide temporary safe places, backup resources, external consultation, and the option to refuse direct dialogue. Withdrawal of supplies, threats, monitoring, and stigma after seeking help trigger anti-retaliation and stopping procedures.

The module can generate only gaps in care or resources, safety boundaries, and candidates for T0–T4. It does not authorize entering a household, contacting children or dependents, changing property or care arrangements, or making decisions about guardianship. It does not substitute for procedures for child protection, medical care, guardianship, or domestic violence.

Scope of domain evidence and downgrading for gaps (partial coverage). The framework’s rules can identify shared living arrangements, the privatization of costs at major life transitions, and protection needs where exit is impossible. The module’s evidence and protocols are incomplete for children, older people, people with disabilities, economically dependent people, and other subdomains. If materials are insufficient, record only risks and facts to verify. Do not presume consent, assign care responsibilities, or propose guardianship or disposition of resources. Child protection, medical, guardianship, or domestic violence procedures must provide further verification.

15.3.2Note

Understanding this section

15.3.2 APP-FAM | Family

Family boundaries require separate checks for the rights, resources, and care at issue; co-residence or “the whole family’s interests” cannot substitute for members’ consent.

Short quotation translated from Chinese: “does not presuppose a single membership boundary capable of uniformly allocating all rights and obligations.” Co-residence, recognized kinship, affection, property, care, labor, and legal eligibility must be separated. Living together does not guarantee shared resource control; care contributions do not automatically confer inheritance eligibility; living in different places does not automatically cancel legal relationships. Specific legal eligibility must be checked in the relevant jurisdiction. The book proposes rules for checking boundaries, not substitutes for legal conclusions. [T-2]

The nuclear family may be a particular statistical category, not the sole real form or normative standard. The family as a whole, relationship dyads, care chains, personal safety incidents, and external institutions are different objects. Birth, death, illness, migration, custody, and changes in economic dependency may all require rechecking boundaries and K. Analytical identity cannot rest solely on the same surname or address. [T-2]

Children, older adults, patients, disabled people, economically dependent people, and primary caregivers are listed separately to prevent inability to exit from being recorded as consent, the health costs of care work from becoming invisible, resource control from being treated as a private matter, and collective interests from cancelling individual rights. Love, filial duty, responsibility, and sacrifice can be normative reasons expressed by the person concerned; others must not appropriate them as commands for unlimited giving. [T-2]

Weak signals may enter through behavioral, indirect, proxy, and delayed expression; vulnerable members must not have to provide the same narrative materials as adults with abundant resources before receiving protection. Low-power members must not be forced to bear the costs of apparent stability; when they cannot leave, temporary safe places, backup resources, external consultation, and refusal of direct dialogue should be available. Withdrawal of support, threats, surveillance, and stigmatization after help-seeking trigger anti-retaliation measures and a halt to steps that increase risk. [T-2]

The module can only identify care/resource gaps, safety boundaries, and candidate T-types. Entering a household, contacting children or dependents, adjusting property or care arrangements, and making guardianship decisions all require the corresponding independent procedures; the claim of acting “for the good of the family” cannot give an analyst permission. Child protection, medical, guardianship, and domestic violence procedures cannot all be replaced by internal family negotiation. [T-2]

Evidence provides partial coverage: rules for ordinary shared living and protection when exit is impossible exist, but subgroup evidence and protocols for the various dependent groups are incomplete. When materials are missing, record risks and facts awaiting verification, defer propositions that depend on them, require domain protocols, and take no external action; presumed consent, assigning care responsibilities, and proposing guardianship or resource dispositions are prohibited. Independently supported criticism of boundaries and procedures may still be retained. [T-2; T-main]

DWP’s 2023–2024 Family Resources Survey distinguishes a co-resident statistical household from a family/benefit unit and records informal carers who care for people outside their household. The statistical household boundary therefore cannot directly serve as the care-network boundary; a benefit unit is not a single definition covering all legal family relationships either. Official classifications and descriptions are used here; survey proportions cannot establish who ought to provide care. [P-FRS]

How the argument develops

  1. 1

    Draw separate boundaries for residence, eligibility, property, labor, and care according to the specific question.

  2. 2

    Recheck K when the object or a life-stage node changes.

  3. 3

    List dependents and caregivers separately, allowing proxy and nonverbal signals.

  4. 4

    Check for control and retaliation after help-seeking, and protect refusal.

  5. 5

    When professional evidence is incomplete, register only the gaps; do not assign care, guardianship, or property decisions.

Distinctions to keep clear

Shared residence

A statistical category or living arrangement.

≠

Shared control of resources

Must be verified separately.

Facts about care

Who actually performs which work.

≠

Legal eligibility

Cannot be automatically established on the basis of contributions.

Apparent stability

Family conflict does not become visible.

≠

Members’ safety

Control, refusal, and exit still need checking.

Teaching construction: three different membership listsTeaching scenario

AssumptionsEntirely constructed scenarios and values, used to test inference ceilings.

A fictional address register lists A, B, and C; the actual care chain also includes D, who lives elsewhere; one property record lists only A. The three lists answer different questions. D’s work cannot be erased because D does not live there, nor can property rights or guardianship be directly changed because D provides care. Facts, norms, and applicable law need separate investigation.

BoundaryNot evidence from a real investigation, professional diagnosis, or effects of intervention.

Different statistical units and care across households in the UK FRSDocumented case

The 2023–2024 survey defines household and family/benefit unit separately and records care provided to people outside the household. Shared residence and care relationships therefore cannot automatically be combined into a single analytical boundary.

15.3.3APP-ORG | Organizations and Projects ​

In briefThe organization module traces the entire chain from goals to feedback and responsibility; identifying a risk does not grant authority to score, appoint, or discipline people.
Codes used in this section (2)
  • T0Carriers of Safety and Trust
  • T4Exit, Transfer, and Preservation of Evolutionary Memory

The object is the chain of objectives, resources, positions, execution, feedback, and responsibility in a specified organization or project. Register the organization, project, department, position, and individual separately. When the object of analysis changes among individual performance, the function of a position, a process, a project, and the organization’s institutional arrangements, rebuild the K mapping.

Key risks include metrics displacing objectives, distortion in summaries at intermediate levels, pushing responsibility downward, invisibility of maintenance and care work, retaliation through performance evaluation against people who give feedback, outsourcing long-term costs through temporary projects, and using framework labels in personnel decisions. Beyond basic diagnosis, midsize organizations should add the chains of return flow and transmission, implementation incentives, carriers for uptake at intermediate levels, frequent small return flows, and channels for disputes that cause little disruption.

Central summaries must not silence frontline workarounds, near misses, maintenance debt, informal complaints, or signs that people may leave. List separately positions weak in contract terms, rank, resources, evaluation, or ability to exit. Where exit is blocked by the industry, income, visas, career history, or care responsibilities, provide representation and external review. Changes in performance ratings, schedules, promotion, contracts, or resources after dissent enter anti-retaliation monitoring.

The module can identify risks, breaks in uptake or return flow, and candidates for T0–T4. It does not authorize scoring, appointment, discipline, layoffs, contract changes, or financial changes. Once diagnosis is used in a personnel decision, the corresponding action must be put on hold, people who provided feedback must be protected, and independent appeal and rollback must be available.

Scope of domain evidence and downgrading for gaps (partial coverage). The framework’s rules support checks on translation across organizational roles and levels, return flows, uptake at intermediate levels, responsibility chains, and concentrations of power. Evidence about the specific industry, position, labor relations, and project cycle still needs external supplementation. If on-site records, data by group, or independent review are missing, findings of fact, causal attributions of responsibility, and eligibility for real-world adoption that depend on them cannot be established. One may propose audit questions, recommendations for reversible trials, and assessments of texts, procedural critiques, and conditional plans that have independent grounds. These do not permit scoring, appointment, discipline, layoffs, or changes to contracts.

15.3.3Note

Understanding this section

15.3.3 APP-ORG | Organizations and Projects

The organization module traces the entire chain from goals to feedback and responsibility; identifying a risk does not grant authority to score, appoint, or discipline people.

Original location: Chinese source lines 3224–3235; original site location /theory/part-15#section-15-3-3. See the theory-v2 source for the current full text; historical research manuscripts and excerpts remain available for download and checking against the original edition.

Short quotation, translated from the Chinese: “Organizations, projects, departments, positions, and individuals must be registered separately.” The object is a specific organization/project’s goals–resources–positions–execution–feedback–responsibility chain. Individual performance, position functions, processes, projects, and organizational institutions influence one another but are not the same object; conversion requires rebuilding the K mapping, and a process gap must not be written directly as a personality defect. [T-3]

Focus on metrics replacing goals, distortion in middle-management summaries, responsibility pushed downward, invisible maintenance and care work, performance-related retaliation, temporary projects outsourcing long-term costs, and framework labels used in personnel actions. Medium-sized organizations also need return-flow chains, transmission chains, execution incentives, middle-management uptake mechanisms, frequent small return flows, and dispute interfaces that cause little disruption. Meeting quarterly KPIs cannot substitute for these chains actually functioning. [T-3]

Frontline workarounds, near misses, maintenance backlogs, informal complaints, and signals preceding resignation must not be silenced by central summaries. List separately positions with little power in contracts, rank, resources, evaluation, or exit; industry, income, visa, employment-history, and care constraints can restrict exit, requiring proxies and external review. Changes to performance evaluations, scheduling, promotion, contracts, or resources after dissent are anti-retaliation signals that trigger investigation, not automatic causal findings. [T-3]

Outputs consist of risks, breaks in uptake/return flow, and candidate T-types; they do not authorize scoring, appointment, discipline, layoffs, or contractual or financial changes. Once a diagnosis is used in a personnel action, that action must be frozen, those providing feedback protected, and independent appeal and rollback allowed. This does not mean the analyst takes over all organizational power; it is the original’s requirement to interrupt a conversion of use that has bypassed the necessary procedures. [T-3]

Partial coverage means that industry, position, labor relations, and project cycles still require external evidence. Without field records, disaggregated data, or independent review, factual findings, causal attribution of responsibility, and eligibility for real-world adoption that depend on them cannot be established; audit questions, reversible pilot suggestions, independently supported criticism of texts/processes, and conditional plans may still be offered. A pilot suggestion is not authorization actually to change schedules or reallocate resources. [T-3; T-main]

The SEC’s 2013 Knight settlement order records a server missed in the 2012 deployment, the lack of a second review, and 97 messages not acted on as warnings. It provides specific, checkable nodes in the deployment, review, information, and response chains. Only findings in the regulatory document are used here; hindsight is not rewritten as an employee’s motives, nor does this case replace field evidence for any other organization. [P-KNIGHT]

How the argument develops

  1. 1

    Distinguish individuals, positions, processes, projects, and organizations.

  2. 2

    Find falsifiable breaks by tracing goals, resources, execution, and return flow.

  3. 3

    Allow frontline and maintenance signals to enter, and protect low-power feedback providers.

  4. 4

    When use shifts to a personnel action, freeze that action and conduct independent review.

  5. 5

    When field evidence is missing, retain questions and conditional plans while suspending factual adjudication and adoption.

Distinctions to keep clear

Metric achieved

A proxy measure reaches its target.

≠

Organizational goal

Actual functions and side effects need checking.

Process defect

Uptake or transmission has not been established.

≠

Individual responsibility

Requires separate facts, causation, and procedure.

Pilot suggestion

A reversible proposal for deliberation.

≠

Implementing the pilot

Still requires choice and authority over resources.

Teaching construction: output and maintenance debtTeaching scenario

AssumptionsEntirely constructed scenarios and values, used to test inference ceilings.

A constructed project delivers 100 items and meets its KPI while leaving 20 maintenance issues unresolved. Achievement of the delivery metric and the maintenance gap can be established separately; without failure, disaggregated, and responsibility records, the 20 issues cannot directly establish someone’s dereliction, nor can the 100 items establish organizational health.

BoundaryNot evidence from a real investigation, professional diagnosis, or effects of intervention.

Can poor departmental metrics directly justify punishing the manager?

No; the object, causation, responsibility, and valid procedures are required, and the module grants no disciplinary authority.

Basis: ORG, object and action ceiling.

Can complaints preceding resignation be excluded because the sample is small?

They cannot be silenced solely on grounds of quantity; they should be examined according to the leads and protection requirements.

Basis: ORG, weak signals.

Can a complete conditional plan be provided?

Yes, with sufficient independent grounds and explicit conditions; eligibility for real-world adoption is checked separately.

Basis: ORG, downgrade when information is missing.

15.3.4APP-PLT | Platforms ​

In briefA platform audit freezes the actual version and distinguishes internal mechanisms from bounded total effects; representational drift does not automatically equal changes in people’s preferences or group harm.
Codes used in this section (2)
  • T0Carriers of Safety and Trust
  • T4Exit, Transfer, and Preservation of Evolutionary Memory

The platform object is the chain of written rules, parameter rules, interface rules, models, distribution, behavioral responses, and data write-back at a frozen version. A public rule alone does not specify it. Register the platform, model, product interface, content network, user groups, and external social impacts separately. Revalidate K when the objective function, parameters, entry point, or model version changes.

Risks include recommendation loops that train on the world they shape, popularity bias, declining diversity, capture by proxy objectives, dual ledgers across text, parameters, and interfaces, automation bias, gates on visibility and eligibility, and control of appeals by the same chain of power. Audit the objective function, parameters, default entry points, human review, behavioral feedback, and effects by group that the current claim requires. Claims about internal mechanisms require the corresponding version and implementation material. Assessing a limited total effect supported by a comparison that meets the requirements does not require access to all internal parameters. Check training write-back only when model retraining actually occurs. Fixed distribution rules can also form feedback.

Material from low-traffic positions, minority groups, people wrongly excluded, and people who left must not be downweighted by count alone. List platform workers, small creators, people without an alternative platform, and people subject to automated decisions separately. Where platform lock-in exists, provide data migration, appeal through a representative, and human review. Throttling, bans, or changes in income after appealing, refusing a data use, or reporting an error are signals for anti-retaliation checks.

The module produces only audit questions about parameters or interfaces, effects by group, and candidates for T0–T4. It does not authorize data access, post deletion, throttling, account bans, changes to models or parameters, or decisions on eligibility for work. Stop expanding use and roll back the version when the object version changes, harm to a group exceeds a threshold, human review is inaccessible, or rollback capability is lost.

Scope of domain evidence and downgrading for gaps (substantial coverage). The rules specify where to check networks, diffusion, conditional potential fields, parameters, recommendation loops, and automated governance. Specific platform mechanisms and effects still require independent evidence.

Research on recommendations should distinguish behavioral records, preference representations within the system, independently measured preferences, and actual consequences. Drift in representations during simulation cannot by itself establish changes in people’s internal preferences or real-world harm to groups (see Mansoury et al., 2020). Changes supported by other independent materials should still be retained. The existence of feedback, amplification of bias, and lock-in that is difficult to correct also require separate evidence.

Suspend an assertion about a parameter or internal mechanism if evidence on the relevant version, parameters, or implementation is insufficient. Randomized or quasi-experimental studies with clearly defined interventions and valid comparisons can support limited effects within their samples, treatments, outcomes, and time windows, even if researchers cannot obtain all internal parameters. Effects of the entire configuration cannot be recorded as independent contributions of its parameters or extrapolated to other versions. Without evidence about effects by group and effective review, do not certify fairness, safety, or eligibility for broader action.

15.3.4Note

Understanding this section

15.3.4 APP-PLT | Platforms

A platform audit freezes the actual version and distinguishes internal mechanisms from bounded total effects; representational drift does not automatically equal changes in people’s preferences or group harm.

Original location: Chinese source lines 3236–3251; original site location /theory/part-15#section-15-3-4. See the theory-v2 source for the current full text; historical research manuscripts and excerpts remain available for download and checking against the original edition.

Short quotation, translated from the Chinese: “The platform object is not a set of public rules.” The object is a version-frozen chain of textual rules–parameter rules–interface rules–model–distribution–behavioral response–data write-back. Register the platform, model, interface, content network, user groups, and external social effects separately; recheck K when the objective function, parameters, entry point, or model version changes, and do not use results from the previous version to cover the current one. [T-4]

Check recommendation loops, popularity bias, diversity, proxy objectives, dual ledgers of textual/parameter/interface rules, automation bias, visibility eligibility gates, and appeals controlled within the same chain. Select objective functions, parameters, default entry points, human review, behavioral feedback, and disaggregated materials according to the claim; indiscriminate collection of all internal information is not required. Check training write-back only when retraining is actually involved; fixed distribution rules can also produce a loop through behavioral feedback. [T-4]

Claims about internal mechanisms require evidence about the corresponding version, parameters, and implementation; randomized or quasi-experiments with suitable comparisons and clearly defined interventions can support bounded total effects within their samples, treatments, outcomes, and time windows, without obtaining every internal parameter as a prerequisite. The effect of the whole configuration must not be separately recorded as each parameter’s independent contribution, or directly extrapolated to other versions. [T-4]

Separate four levels: behavioral records, preference representations within the system, independently measured preferences, and actual consequences. Mansoury et al.’s 2020 offline simulation used MovieLens and generated subsequent interactions to observe system representations; §4.3.2 explicitly states that a change in representation is not a change in inherent preferences. It can support results of the specified simulated mechanism, but does not by itself establish psychological changes in real people, real-world group harm, or lock-in that is difficult to correct. [T-4; P-MANS]

Gather separate evidence for the existence of feedback, amplification of bias, and lock-in; drawing a loop arrow does not establish all three. The fact that this simulation cannot establish psychological change must not be used to deny changes that other independent materials might support. Nor must all clearly defined bounded total effects be treated as unknowable because internal parameters are missing. [T-4]

Do not reduce the weight of materials concerning low-traffic users, minorities, false positives, or those who exit on grounds of quantity; list separately platform workers, small creators, people without alternative platforms, and subjects of automated decisions. Lock-in requires data migration, proxy appeals, and human review; changes in traffic limits, bans, or income following appeals, refusal of data uses, or error reports enter anti-retaliation review, without being treated directly as established causation. [T-4]

The module generates only audit questions, disaggregated impacts, and candidate T-types; it does not authorize data access, post deletion, traffic restrictions, account bans, changes to model parameters, or changes to labor eligibility. When the version changes, group harm crosses a threshold, human review becomes inaccessible, or rollback capacity disappears, stop scaling and roll back through valid procedures. What is marked as substantively covered is the set of rule-checking positions; the mechanisms and effects of a particular platform still require independent evidence. Without disaggregated and review materials, do not certify fairness, safety, or eligibility for expanded action. [T-4; T-main]

How the argument develops

  1. 1

    Freeze the object chain and version to prevent rule texts from substituting for implementation.

  2. 2

    Match evidence to claims about mechanisms or total effects.

  3. 3

    Separate behavior, representation, independent preferences, and actual consequences.

  4. 4

    Protect low-volume groups and appeals, and check harm by group.

  5. 5

    Without mechanism evidence, suspend that claim; retain supported bounded effects, and check expanded action separately.

Distinctions to keep clear

Feedback under fixed rules

Behavior can return to system inputs or the environment.

≠

Training write-back

Claim it only when retraining actually occurs.

Representational drift

The preference representation in system records has changed.

≠

Change in inherent preferences

Requires independent measurement, not an inference from simulation.

Total effect of the entire intervention

A bounded comparison of the treatment in a specified version.

≠

Contribution of a single parameter

Requires additional identification.

Substantive coverage

The framework contains corresponding checking positions.

≠

Complete empirical evidence

Still requires evidence for the particular platform.

Teaching construction: type proportions in recordsTeaching scenario

AssumptionsEntirely constructed scenarios and values, used to test inference ceilings.

A constructed profile initially contains 4 type-A records and 6 type-B records; a fixed rule then exposes and records 4 more A items, changing A’s share from 4/10=40% to 8/14≈57.1%. This establishes a change in recorded proportions under the setup; without independent preference measurement, one cannot assert that a person’s inherent preferences changed in the same proportion, or that the rule was retrained.

BoundaryNot evidence from a real investigation, professional diagnosis, or effects of intervention.

Mansoury et al.’s 2020 offline feedback simulationDocumented case

The study uses MovieLens data and offline-generated interactions to study changes in popularity and representation; §4.3.2 specifically distinguishes preference representations within the system from inherent preferences.

SourceMansoury and colleagues: Feedback Loop and Bias Amplification in Recommender SystemsarXiv:2007.13019v1, §2 and §§4.1–4.3.2 (PDF pages 2–3)Reading scope: Partly read

Scope and limitsThis is an original simulation study, not a field intervention on a real platform; the code was not rerun, and it is not used to adjudicate actual psychological or group harm.

Can observing a feedback loop directly establish lock-in?

No; amplification and difficulty of correction require separate evidence.

Basis: PLT, evidence levels.

If all parameters cannot be obtained, do all causal effects fail to hold?

No; suitable definitions and comparisons can support the corresponding bounded total effect.

Basis: PLT, final paragraph.

If simulated preference profiles change, do psychological preferences change too?

Not automatically; independent measurement is required, and the simulation supports only its representation and generation conditions.

Basis: Mansoury §4.3.2 and PLT.

15.3.5APP-INS | Institutions and Public Governance ​

In briefPublic governance verifies law, implementation, budgets, and affected people separately; an institutional evaluation can hold, while public action still requires independent authority.
Codes used in this section (2)
  • T0Carriers of Safety and Trust
  • T4Exit, Transfer, and Preservation of Evolutionary Memory

The object is the structure of institutional rules, execution, resources, eligibility, feedback, responsibility, and public commitments within a frozen jurisdiction and time window. Register legal texts, policies, implementing institutions, budgets, informal rules, public objects, and affected groups separately. A state, institution, organization, and policy are distinct objects.

Major risks include shared sources for key channels, closure around concentrated power, filtering of bad news, backlash after appeals, pushing responsibility downward, oversight captured by beneficiaries of a rule, paper compliance standing in for reality, public commitments extracting sacrifice, majorities and stability overriding rights, and romanticizing multiple centers or autonomy. Legal validity and normative justification must be kept separate. Public benefits must be broken down by group, region, generation, and ability to exit.

Aggregate metrics must not silence downstream positions, minorities, regions at the margins, informal practices, and absence signals. List separately positions weak in rights, resources, eligibility, information, or ability to exit. People unable to exit a public institution or essential service need representation, alternative services, and external review. Administrative, occupational, service, eligibility, and reputational changes after reporting wrongdoing, mounting a defense, or appealing enter anti-retaliation audits.

The module can produce institutional risks, distributional impacts, gaps in procedure, stress tests, and candidates for T0–T4. It does not authorize legislation, law enforcement, budgets, eligibility decisions, regulation, or disposition of public resources. Stop and roll back if appeals and review are controlled by the same chain of power, rights floors are breached, temporary measures become permanent, or the framework is used as a veneer of legitimacy.

Scope of domain evidence and downgrading for gaps (substantial coverage). The rules cover checks on concentrations of power, production and distribution, public commitments, multiple centers, bureaucracy, and misuse. Specific institutions still require case registration, comparison across jurisdictions, and causal evaluation. If evidence about applicable law, implementation, budgets, or affected groups is missing, stop each legal finding, certification of effects, or real-world adoption that depends on the gap. The framework cannot be used to prove a political position or issue authorization for public action. Independently grounded critiques of texts, institutional evaluations under explicit normative premises, and complete drafts of charters and plans for review can still stand. State the conditions of applicability, costs, and matters awaiting review for each item.

15.3.5Note

Understanding this section

15.3.5 APP-INS | Institutions and Public Governance

Public governance verifies law, implementation, budgets, and affected people separately; an institutional evaluation can hold, while public action still requires independent authority.

Original location: Chinese source lines 3252–3263; original site location /theory/part-15#section-15-3-5. See the theory-v2 source for the current full text; historical research manuscripts and excerpts remain available for download and checking against the original edition.

Short quotation, translated from the Chinese: “Legal validity and normative justification must be separated.” Freeze the object’s jurisdiction and time window, and trace institutional rules–implementation–resources–eligibility–feedback–responsibility–public commitments. Register legal texts, policies, implementing agencies, budgets, informal rules, public objects, and affected groups separately; state, institution, organization, and policy are not synonymous objects. [T-5]

Risks include key channels sharing a source, closure by those with high power, filtering of bad news, appeals backfiring, responsibility pushed downward, beneficiaries capturing oversight, documentary compliance substituting for reality, public commitments appropriating sacrifice, majority stability suppressing rights, and romanticizing polycentric self-governance. Replacing one oversight signboard with several does not ensure independence in their funding, appointments, information, or corrective powers. [T-5]

Public benefits must be disaggregated by group, region, generation, and capacity to exit. Signals from the end of the chain, minorities, margins, informal practices, and absences must not be silenced by aggregate figures; list separately positions with limited rights, resources, eligibility, information, or exit capacity. People unable to exit basic institutions/services need proxies, alternative services, and external review; “they can move away” must not be used to evade existing protection responsibilities. [T-5]

Administrative, occupational, service, eligibility, and reputational changes following reporting, defense, or appeal enter anti-retaliation audits. The module may identify risks, distributional impacts, procedural gaps, stress tests, and candidate T-types; it does not authorize legislation, enforcement, decisions over budgets or eligibility, regulation, or disposition of public resources. When appeals and reviews are controlled by the same chain, rights floors are breached, temporary measures become permanent, or the framework is used to dress up legitimacy, the relevant adoption must stop and be rolled back. [T-5]

Substantive coverage locates rule-level checks for concentrated power, distribution, public commitments, polycentric bureaucracy, and misuse. Specific institutions still require cases, jurisdictional comparison, and causal evaluation. Missing applicable law, execution data, budgets, or group evidence suspends the legal determinations, effectiveness certifications, and real-world adoption judgments that depend on them, item by item; the framework does not certify political positions. [T-5]

Independently grounded textual criticism, institutional evaluation under explicit norms, and complete charters or plans for review can be valid outputs; they need not retreat into mere question lists. State applicability conditions, prices to be paid, and review items individually. A draft for review is not an institution in force, and complete prose cannot fill resource or permission gaps. [T-5；T-main]

Recommendation 15.1 on Australia's 2023 Robodebt Royal Commission website distinguishes legislation required for lawful implementation from spending authorization. Recommendation 17.1 requires review paths and transparency material for automated decisions. This lesson only compares distinctions in duties expressed by those public recommendations. The full report was not read, and the recommendation list does not establish that reforms were executed or improved people's circumstances. [P-ROBO]

How the argument develops

  1. 1

    Freeze the jurisdictional window; distinguish text, implementation, budgets, and informal rules.

  2. 2

    Check public commitments against sources of power and group costs.

  3. 3

    Check independent appeals, protection for those unable to exit, and protection against retaliation.

  4. 4

    Use gaps to bound legal/effectiveness/adoption judgments.

  5. 5

    Retain proposals for review under explicit norms; prohibit treating the framework as a license for action.

Distinctions to keep clear

Legal validity

Holds in the applicable jurisdiction.

≠

Normative justification

Requires independent public reasons.

Polycentric label

Multiple institutions exist.

≠

Independent correction

Requires checking control, resources, and ability to act.

Charter for review

A complete text for deliberation.

≠

Institution in force

Separately requires lawful procedures and permissions.

Teaching construction: procedural text and implementation factsTeaching scenario

AssumptionsEntirely constructed scenarios and values, used to test inference ceilings.

A fictional regulation promises appeal responses within 7 days, and its clarity can be reviewed as text. Without actual submission, response, review, and group records, one cannot claim the institution effectively remedies everyone's case within 7 days. A complete amendment draft can be proposed, but cannot directly change eligibility or budgets.

BoundaryNot evidence from a real investigation, professional diagnosis, or effects of intervention.

Recommendation 15.1 on the report website explicitly distinguishes lawful implementation from spending authorization; 17.1 proposes review paths, explanations, and material for independent scrutiny of automated decisions.

Does criticizing an existing institution first require enforcement authority?

No. Grounded criticism and normative evaluation can be valid; authority to act is checked separately.

Basis: INS missingness downgrade.

Can majority support replace minimum rights protections?

Not automatically; independent normative and protective reasons are required.

Basis: INS risk items.

Does a recommendation list prove implementation?

No. Evidence of execution, resources, and actual impact is still needed.

Basis: The limited source boundary of P-ROBO.
