15.3.6APP-OPI | Public Opinion ​

In briefPublic-opinion analysis separates visibility, exposure, judgment, expression, and action layer by layer; attention cannot substitute for facts, the public population, or justification.
Codes used in this section (2)
  • T0Carriers of Safety and Trust
  • T4Exit, Transfer, and Preservation of Evolutionary Memory

The object is a process of public interpretation with the event, issue, groups, propagation network, platform conditions, and time window frozen. Facts, evidence, recognition, interpretation, responsibility, identity, and action must be kept at separate levels. Popularity does not establish who the public is or what is representative of it.

Major risks include substituting popularity for facts and agreement, creating false agreement by deleting comments or throttling, labeling critics as mechanisms of destabilization, substituting apologies for compensation, platform rewards for conflict, simple diffusion producing wide attention with little uptake, and forcing people affected to prove their circumstances publicly. The purpose of responding is to reduce factual confusion, obscured responsibility, loss of trust, and gaps in repair. It does not aim to suppress attention.

Low-attention material, expression from the margins, deleted material, silence, and absence enter as weak signals. List separately positions without agenda-setting or public relations resources and those bearing identity exposure. People unable to exit public exposure receive representation for speaking, reduced exposure, and correction of records. Online abuse, throttling, and changes in employment or resources after speaking up enter anti-retaliation monitoring.

The module produces only levels of clarification, gaps in evidence, questions about repair, and candidates for T0–T4. It does not authorize deleting comments, throttling, controlling comments, publishing individual material, or classifying the public as a whole. Stop and publish a traceable correction when a factual version changes, the response increases exposure, a platform action exceeds authority, or corrections cannot be written back into the propagation chain.

Scope of domain evidence and downgrading for gaps (partial coverage). Record separately material eligible to enter the candidate content set, actual presentation, reading or contact, private judgments, public expression, and verifiable actions. Deletion and editing, media choice, shared events, and existing relations can all change the visible distribution. A change in exposure with no detected change in attitudes does not cancel the effect on exposure or establish permanent ineffectiveness. Popularity and participation counts use denominators for platform behavior. Public opinion requires its own population and sampling. Public legitimacy also requires independent normative and institutional grounds. If materials are insufficient, suspend claims about representativeness, mechanisms, or effects that depend on the gap. Independently grounded text evaluations, local facts, and conditional recommendations can be retained, with traceable correction available.

15.3.6Note

Understanding this section

15.3.6 APP-OPI | Public Opinion

Public-opinion analysis separates visibility, exposure, judgment, expression, and action layer by layer; attention cannot substitute for facts, the public population, or justification.

Short quotation translated from Chinese: “Attention is not the public, nor is it representativeness.” Freeze the event, issue, groups, communication network, platform conditions, and window, separating facts, evidence, acknowledgment, explanation, responsibility, identity, and action. Many posts indicate only a volume of behavior on a platform; they do not directly establish public consensus, factual truth, or who has decision rights. [T-6]

Main risks include false consensus through comment deletion or reach restriction, labeling critics as destabilizing mechanisms, substituting apologies for compensation, rewarding conflict, intense diffusion without adequate uptake, and forcing affected people to publicly prove themselves. The response aims to reduce factual confusion, obscured responsibility, damaged trust, and missing repair—not merely lower a curve. Public acknowledgment and repair action differ; each can progress without impersonating the other. [T-6]

Low attention, marginal expression, deleted material, silence, and absence can all be weak signals. Separately record positions lacking agenda-setting or public-relations resources and those bearing identity exposure. People unable to exit public exposure should have access to proxy expression, reduced exposure, and record correction. Online abuse, reach restrictions, and changes in occupational resources after speaking enter retaliation monitoring; evidence requirements must not force another public disclosure of sensitive experiences. [T-6]

Domain evidence provides partial coverage. Separately record content eligible for candidacy, actual presentation, reading/exposure, private judgment, public expression, and verifiable action. Deletions and edits, media selection, shared events, and existing relationships can all alter visible distributions. Specify denominators and comparison conditions; do not attribute all observed change to one recommendation mechanism. [T-6]

Changed exposure without a detected attitude change does not erase the exposure effect or prove permanent ineffectiveness. Attention and engagement use platform-behavior denominators; public opinion needs a separately defined population and sampling; public justification needs separate normative and institutional grounds. The authors' institutional summary of Guess et al. 2023 reports that feed treatment changed platform experience in a three-month study in 2020, while several attitude indicators did not change significantly. This limited information already illustrates why distinct endpoints cannot be merged. [T-6；P-GUESS]

The module generates only clarification layers, gaps, repair questions, and candidate T types. It does not authorize comment deletion, reach restriction, comment manipulation, disclosure of personal material, or definitive labeling of the public. If factual versions change, responses increase exposure, platform actions exceed authority, or corrections cannot be written back through the dissemination chain, stop the relevant steps and issue traceable corrections. A correction should state what changed, the original version, and current grounds rather than silently replacing text. [T-6]

When material is missing, suspend representativeness, mechanism, or effectiveness conclusions that depend on the gap; independently supported textual evaluation, local facts, and conditional recommendations can remain. This lesson read only the Guess authors' institutional summary because the journal full text was inaccessible. It therefore makes no claims about randomization, subgroup estimates, statistical power, or subsequent long-term effects. This is itself a concrete example of gaps limiting output. [T-6；P-GUESS]

How the argument develops

  1. 1

    Fix the event, groups, platform, and time window.

  2. 2

    Separate candidate content, presentation, exposure, judgment, expression, and action.

  3. 3

    Set denominators and comparisons by proposition; do not substitute attention for the population.

  4. 4

    Protect exposed positions and the correction dissemination chain.

  5. 5

    Separate nonsignificance from ineffectiveness; gaps limit only the corresponding representativeness/mechanism/effectiveness claims.

Distinctions to keep clear

Exposure effect

The distribution of content seen changes.

≠

Attitude effect

Private judgments change; this requires separate measurement.

No significant change detected

Evidence is limited under the given sample and measurement.

≠

Permanent zero effect

Does not follow automatically.

Attention denominator

Activity or content volume on the platform.

≠

Public population

Requires a separately defined population and sampling.

Apology

An act acknowledging or expressing responsibility.

≠

Remedy

The harmed position actually receives repair.

Teaching construction: candidacy, presentation, and reading differTeaching scenario

AssumptionsEntirely constructed scenarios and values, used to test inference ceilings.

Of 100 constructed candidate content items, 60 are presented, 20 have exposure records, and 12 people reply publicly. 100, 60, 20, and 12 refer to different stages and potentially different units. The 12 respondents' opinions cannot be treated as the “public opinion” of 100 content items, much less that of all city residents.

BoundaryNot evidence from a real investigation, professional diagnosis, or effects of intervention.

Different outcome endpoints in the 2020 feed studyDocumented case

The authors' institutional summary of Guess et al.'s 2023 paper reports that reverse-chronological feeds changed usage and content exposure during the 2020 US election, while several attitude indicators did not change significantly within three months.

SourceGuess et al.: How do social media feed algorithms affect attitudes and behavior in an election campaign?Abstract on the authors’ NetSI institutional publication page, web page lines 13–15; Science 381:398–404Reading scope: Partly read

Scope and limitsBased only on the summary; does not claim the full text was read or that long-term ineffectiveness was proved. Platform experience, attitudes, and public justification are not merged into one endpoint.

What does not follow

  • Teaching counterexample: a high support rate after deleting 100 dissenting comments cannot establish public consensus.
  • Source-text boundary: failing to detect attitude change does not cancel an observed change in exposure.
  • Source-text boundary: corrections must be traceable; silently overwriting the old version cannot be called correction.

Scope and open questions

Cases serve local factual or institutional comparisons; theoretical rules, original evidence, teaching constructions, and unresolved authority are labeled separately.

  • This lesson undertakes no execution in a real setting; professional protocols, field facts, valid authorization, and protective effects require separate verification.
  • External evidence supports only the propositions listed in the source table; material titles do not fill unread portions or unmeasured effects.

Check your understanding

  1. 1

    Does low attention mean a response is unwarranted?

  2. 2

    If exposure changes but attitudes do not change significantly, did nothing happen?

  3. 3

    May a person's information be disclosed directly for clarification?

Does low attention mean a response is unwarranted?

Volume alone cannot justify lower priority; evaluate evidence, harm, and affected positions.

Basis: OPI weak signals.

If exposure changes but attitudes do not change significantly, did nothing happen?

No. Exposure and attitude endpoints are assessed separately.

Basis: OPI missingness downgrade.

May a person's information be disclosed directly for clarification?

The module does not authorize disclosure; corresponding consent, necessity, and permissions are required.

Basis: OPI action ceiling.

15.3.7APP-SPC | Space and Channels ​

In briefSpatial connections require segment-by-segment verification along actual use paths and tracking the same households. Maps and area averages cannot substitute for recovery of everyday life.
Codes used in this section (2)
  • T0Carriers of Safety and Trust
  • T4Exit, Transfer, and Preservation of Evolutionary Memory

The object is a network of space and channels with coordinates, functional meanings, population/users, time window, and layers of dependency frozen. Register physical locations, functional networks, administrative boundaries, service areas, and infrastructure layers separately. A connection on a map does not establish adequate capacity, substitutability, or actual access.

Risks include concentration of key nodes, overload at the center and disconnection at the margins, infrastructure failures with common causes, inadequate capacity and alternative routes, and changes to space shifting exposure and relocation costs. Verify the continuous path from actual points of departure to use of a service. Check road connections, times of day, fares, eligibility, physical and informational accessibility, and conditions for remaining at or using the site. Counts of facilities or geometric distance cannot substitute for this. Track original residents before the change, current residents, those who moved out, new arrivals, and those waiting to enter separately. A rise in an area average may result from population replacement and cannot be retroactively attributed to gains for original households. Check plans, conditions on site, and lived experience against one another. For local participation, also check who is absent and who can change the decision.

Breaks at the margins, maintenance workarounds, local congestion, and near misses are weak signals. List separately positions with limited mobility, health, income, digital access, or ability to speak. People unable to relocate or take a different route receive minimum services, alternative channels, and local safe places. Reporting infrastructure risks and refusing unsafe passage are protected against retaliation.

The module produces only requirements for maps, questions about protecting key channels, and candidates for T0–T4. It does not authorize road closures, population relocation, land requisition, allocation of public resources, or engineering changes. Stop and restore channels and services if on-site conditions conflict with the map, alternative routes are not operating, or the changes increase harm at the margins.

Scope of domain evidence and downgrading for gaps (substantial coverage). The rules cover the spatial expression of potential fields, bottlenecks, centers and margins, layers of infrastructure, and the geography of recovery. Engineering safety, capacity thresholds, and on-site usability still require appropriate professional evidence. If a key parameter is unknown, suspend any judgment about channel safety or engineering feasibility that depends on it, and specify the site investigation and measurements needed. Other distributional facts, disputes over rights, or procedural evaluations with independent grounds remain. A map cannot authorize closures, relocation, or resource allocation, and on-site measurements alone do not determine the justified objectives of a change.

For urban development, housing, or reconstruction after a disaster, establish protected links among pre-disaster addresses, current locations, and destinations. Record separately building safety and renewed exposure, services households actually receive, the same residents’ relationship networks, local memory, and whether there is adequate information, feasible choice, and access to appeal and remedy. A well-kept streetscape, open facilities, signs of mail delivery, occupied plots, or an area average cannot substitute for the return of original residents, affordable housing, restored relationships, or authorization to represent others.

For comparisons across locations, group original residents, people who moved out, newcomers, renters, owners, caregivers, people waiting, and people unable to move. Record costs, times, capacity, alternative routes, risks at the destination, and who can change the plan. Connections on a map do not authorize relocation, land acquisition, closures, or resource allocation. If key on-site parameters are missing, the output can specify only the required site investigations and evidence. It must not conclude that a channel is safe or an engineering plan feasible.

15.3.7Note

Understanding this section

15.3.7 APP-SPC | Space and Channels

Spatial connections require segment-by-segment verification along actual use paths and tracking the same households. Maps and area averages cannot substitute for recovery of everyday life.

Short quotation translated from Chinese: “A ‘connection’ on a map does not mean sufficient capacity, substitutability, or actual accessibility.” Freeze coordinates, functional meaning, users, time windows, and dependency layers; separately record physical locations, functional networks, administrative boundaries, service areas, and infrastructure layers. A connection graph can be correct without answering whether a particular group can actually use a service now. [T-7]

Main risks include concentration of key nodes, overloaded centers, disconnected peripheries, common infrastructure failures, inadequate substitute capacity, and spatial redevelopment shifting exposure and relocation costs. Two purported routes depending on the same unpowered pumping station or entrance are not independent alternatives. Substitute capacity must be tested under specific failure conditions, not certified by line count. [T-7]

From an actual origin to actual service use, continuously check routes, operating times, fares, eligibility, physical and informational access, and conditions for staying/using the service. Facility counts, geometric distance, and occupancy of a site cannot skip these links. OECD urban transport indicators explicitly separate distance-based proximity from time/mode-based accessibility and note that a stop's existence may not provide sufficient opportunities. That indicator still does not establish individual affordability, quality, and disability access together. [T-7；P-OECD]

Track pre-renewal residents, current residents, movers, newcomers, and those waiting to enter separately. A higher area average may reflect population replacement rather than benefits to original households. Cross-check planning representations, engineering sites, and lived experience. For participatory meetings, ask who is absent and who can change decisions; attendance does not automatically confer representative authorization. [T-7]

Peripheral breaks, maintenance detours, congestion, and near misses are weak signals. Separately identify positions with limited mobility, health, income, digital access, or ability to express themselves. Those unable to relocate or take detours need minimum services, alternative channels, and local safe points. Reporting facility risks or refusing dangerous passage should not invite retaliation. Additional journeys and time borne by maintainers and carers must not disappear behind average speeds on main roads. [T-7]

The module generates only mapping requirements, key-channel protection questions, and candidate T types. It does not authorize road closures, relocation, land acquisition, public-resource allocation, or engineering changes. Where the site conflicts with the map, alternatives are not operating, or redevelopment increases peripheral harm, stop the relevant actions and restore channel services within authorized scope. Substantive coverage locates rules for spatialization, bottlenecks, overlapping layers, and recovery geography; it is not an engineering-safety qualification. [T-7]

When key site parameters are unknown, suspend channel-safety or engineering-feasibility judgments that depend on them and formulate survey and measurement requirements. Independently established distributional facts, rights disputes, and procedural evaluations remain. Site measurements alone also do not establish the normative justification of redevelopment targets: facts describe consequences but do not automatically decide who should bear relocation costs. [T-7；T-main]

For cities, housing, or post-disaster reconstruction, a protected correspondence among pre-disaster address, current residence, and destination is needed. Separately record building safety/re-exposure, household services, networks among the same residents, local memory, information, feasible options, and appeal remedies. Streetscapes, facility openings, mailing evidence, occupied plots, or area averages cannot substitute for original residents' return, affordable housing, relationship recovery, or representation. [T-7]

For cross-location comparisons, further distinguish original residents, movers, newcomers, tenants, owners, carers, waiters, and those unable to relocate. Record costs, operating times, capacity, alternatives, destination risks, and who can change the plan. Address-linkage data are themselves sensitive and should be protected rather than used to publish person-tracking maps. This lesson contains teaching diagrams only, with no actual household data. [T-7]

How the argument develops

  1. 1

    Freeze coordinates, functions, groups, time, and dependency layers.

  2. 2

    Check accessibility segment by segment from origin to actual service.

  3. 3

    Track the same households and moving groups to avoid substitution by averages.

  4. 4

    Combine planning, engineering, and lived-experience material; protect absent/low-power positions.

  5. 5

    Missing parameters suspend engineering-safety conclusions; separate facts from justified targets and authority to act.

Distinctions to keep clear

Geometric proximity

A facility is nearby.

≠

Actual accessibility

Also requires routes, costs, eligibility, timing, and usability conditions.

Current area average

The average for those living here now.

≠

Benefits to original households

Requires tracking the same people over time.

Alternative line

Another route on the map.

≠

Independent uptake

Requires checking capacity and common failures.

Site parameters

Support technical judgments.

≠

Relocation justification and permissions

Require separate evidence of norms, choices, and authorization.

Teaching construction: an improved average from replacing the denominatorTeaching scenario

AssumptionsEntirely constructed scenarios and values, used to test inference ceilings.

A fictional area originally contains two households with resource amounts 2 and 4, averaging 3. Both later move out, and newcomers have 8 and 10, giving a current average of 9. 9>3 describes averages of two different sets; it does not establish that each original household gained 6. Track original households' new homes, costs, services, and relationship networks; an area map cannot fill those gaps.

BoundaryNot evidence from a real investigation, professional diagnosis, or effects of intervention.

Teaching construction: two routes with one shared breakTeaching scenario

AssumptionsEntirely constructed scenarios and values, used to test inference ceilings.

A constructed map shows routes A/B from home to a service station, but both end through the same unusable gate. Drawing two lines provides no actual alternative. Even with a new independent entrance, missing capacity or opening-time information yields at most a proposal awaiting testing, not a safe-passage conclusion.

BoundaryNot evidence from a real investigation, professional diagnosis, or effects of intervention.

Explicit conventions in OECD urban accessibility indicatorsDocumented case

Chapter 2 of Transport Bridging Divides distinguishes the number of opportunities within a distance from opportunities accessible within a given time/by a given transport mode, and notes that a public-transport stop alone does not establish accessibility to service opportunities.

What does not follow

  • Teaching counterexample: a hospital is 500 meters away, but the route lacks an accessible entrance and a usable alternative. Distance does not prove accessibility for this user.

Scope and open questions

Cases serve local factual or institutional comparisons; theoretical rules, original evidence, teaching constructions, and unresolved authority are labeled separately.

  • This lesson undertakes no execution in a real setting; professional protocols, field facts, valid authorization, and protective effects require separate verification.
  • External evidence supports only the propositions listed in the source table; material titles do not fill unread portions or unmeasured effects.

Check your understanding

  1. 1

    Can more facilities prove recovery for original residents?

  2. 2

    Does missing capacity data also invalidate criticism of opaque procedures?

  3. 3

    If measurements prove a route passable, may people immediately be relocated?

Can more facilities prove recovery for original residents?

No. Corresponding endpoints are needed for the same people, actual services, burdens, relationships, and rights.

Basis: SPC's final two paragraphs.

Does missing capacity data also invalidate criticism of opaque procedures?

No. Only safety and feasibility judgments dependent on capacity are suspended; grounded procedural evaluation remains.

Basis: SPC missingness downgrade.

If measurements prove a route passable, may people immediately be relocated?

No. Relocation targets, choices, and permissions require separate checks.

Basis: SPC action ceiling.

15.3.8APP-EMG | Emergencies and High-Pressure Situations ​

In briefEmergency response follows actual endpoints at each phase and independent professional authority. Lifesaving must not wait for structural analysis, and unfinished recovery does not automatically extend special powers.

The object is a system under high pressure within a specified incident phase, with defined hazards, critical functions, the command chain, information chain, and resource chain, affected areas, and a recovery window. Register the hazard, incident system, response organization, critical functions, and residents’ living conditions separately. Rescue is judged by whether time-sensitive protection of life and against serious harm reaches people. Stabilization is judged by the spread of harm and minimum services. Repair is judged by whether specified functions are usable under explicit conditions. Reconstruction separately checks longer-term facilities, livelihoods, and renewed exposure. Tasks can run in parallel or recur. They cannot share a single success criterion, deadline, or authorization.

In recovery, register rescue, stabilization, functional repair, reconstruction, and long-term recovery of living conditions separately. Building completion, occupancy of an area, and facility operation are distinct endpoints from service availability, housing burden, relationship networks, local memory, and residents’ decision-making authority. “Partial recovery” describes only an observable combination in which some facilities or housing have improved while services, affordability, social connections, or rights are still lacking. It must not be described as a feedback trap without evidence across periods and consideration of competing explanations.

Time pressure in an emergency does not cancel protection of people affected or confer on-site authority on the model. External statutory duties and professional procedure cards determine life-saving, evacuation, dispatch, and engineering actions. The framework only records phases, delays, people unable to evacuate, and gaps in care and appeal. When action exceeds authority, exceptional powers expire, or on-site information overturns assumptions, stop expanding the action and restore ordinary procedures.

Risks include cascades from complex interactions and tight coupling, alert fatigue, accumulation of workarounds and near misses, drift into failure under pressure for efficiency, multiple chains of command, indefinite extension of emergency powers, shifting the costs of narrowing functions, and breaks in the chain of recovery after rescue. The framework recognizes professional emergency authority first. Structural analysis must not delay life-saving action.

Near misses, on-site dissent, low-level alerts, and interruptions of supply at the margins must not be ignored because disaster has yet to occur. Prioritize recording people who cannot decide whether to evacuate, people with impaired mobility, people with limited information, and low-authority frontline positions. People unable to evacuate receive minimum supplies, alternative arrangements for taking over, and representation. Reporting danger, refusing unsafe orders, and appealing afterward are protected against retaliation.

The module can support recording risks, narrowing functions, and continuity of recovery. It does not substitute for medical, firefighting, engineering, or on-site command procedures, or confer authority to evacuate, dispatch, or take action. Temporary centralized coordination can align objectives, information, and resource interfaces. On-site discretion still requires an explicit scope of delegation, professional boundaries, and feedback on anomalies. Check separately the handover of command, winding down of coordinating bodies, termination of each statutory exceptional power, continuity of essential services, and long-term recovery of living conditions. Completing one step does not establish completion of the next, and unfinished recovery does not automatically extend all exceptional powers. When professional information from the site overturns the framework’s assumptions, the framework should return to recording and reviewing events. Expiry, actions beyond authority, and restoration of ordinary procedures must be handled individually under the corresponding powers and tasks.

Recovery can reach different endpoints in phases. If a temporary teaching site, transportation, teachers, and the term budget are all in place, education for this term can genuinely be restored. The original school building need not already have been rebuilt for that outcome to be real. But if no one is in place to take over the site rent and care work next month, opening classes today does not establish stability for the entire term. A later shock also does not automatically negate an earlier limited outcome. “False recovery” first describes a claim exceeding its evidence. It does not presume a motive to deceive. 〔Studies 31.10–31.11, teaching scenario〕

Scope of domain evidence and downgrading for gaps (substantial coverage). The rules cover normal accidents, near misses, drift into failure, narrowing of functions, command, and chains of recovery. Specific disaster types, danger thresholds, statutory command, and professional operating cards must come from the relevant domain systems. Without on-site confirmation, a responsible professional, or valid emergency authorization, the framework only records information and flags risks. It must not delay life-saving action, substitute for command, or generate operational orders.

15.3.8Note

Understanding this section

15.3.8 APP-EMG | Emergencies and High Pressure

Emergency response follows actual endpoints at each phase and independent professional authority. Lifesaving must not wait for structural analysis, and unfinished recovery does not automatically extend special powers.

Short quotation translated from Chinese: “Structural analysis must not delay lifesaving action.” Freeze the incident phase, hazard sources, key functions, command/information/resource chains, area, and recovery window. Hazard sources, incident systems, emergency organizations, key functions, and residents' lives differ. Rescue, stabilization, repair, and reconstruction may run in parallel or recur; they do not share one success criterion, deadline, or authorization. [T-8]

Rescue asks whether time-sensitive protection of life and against serious injury arrives; stabilization asks about expanding harm and minimum services; functional repair asks whether a specified function is usable under explicit conditions; reconstruction asks about long-term facilities, livelihoods, and re-exposure. Long-term life recovery separately asks about services, burdens, relationships, memory, and residents' decision rights. Building completion, area occupancy, and facility operation cannot jointly substitute for these later endpoints. [T-8]

“Partial recovery” refers to an observable combination in which facilities or housing have improved while services, burdens, social relations, or rights remain unresolved. Calling it a feedback trap additionally requires tracking across periods and competing explanations. Persistent hardship does not automatically justify drawing a self-reinforcing loop, nor may deception be presumed. So-called false recovery first means a claim exceeding the scope of its evidence. [T-8]

Time pressure does not cancel protection or give a model authority at the scene. Statutory duties and professional operational cards determine lifesaving, evacuation, dispatch, and engineering actions; the framework records stages, delays, people unable to evacuate, and gaps in care and appeal. If actions exceed authority, special powers expire, or conditions at the scene overturn assumptions, stop the relevant expansion and restore ordinary procedures according to the specific power. Evidence completion under the framework must not become a prerequisite for professional lifesaving action. [T-8]

Risks include tightly coupled cascades of complex interactions, alarm fatigue, accumulated near misses from rule circumvention, drift under efficiency pressure, multiple command centers, indefinite extensions of emergency powers, shifted costs of functional contraction, and broken uptake after rescue. Near misses, on-site dissent, low-level alarms, and service interruptions at the margins must not be discarded because no disaster has yet occurred. Prioritize registration of those unable to decide on evacuation, those with mobility or information limitations, and frontline people with little authority. [T-8]

People unable to evacuate need minimum provision, alternative uptake, and proxies; reporting danger, refusing unsafe orders, and post-event appeals require anti-retaliation protection. The module supports risk records, functional contraction, and continuity of recovery; it does not replace on-site medical, fire, or engineering command or generate evacuation and dispatch authority. Central coordination may unify objectives and interfaces for information and resources, while on-site discretion still requires explicit delegation, professional boundaries, and feedback on anomalies. [T-8]

Command transfer, coordination-body closeout, termination of each statutory special power, continuity of critical services, and long-term recovery of everyday life require separate checks. Completing an earlier item does not automatically establish completion of a later one; unfinished recovery does not automatically extend every special power. When on-site professional information overturns the framework's assumptions, the framework steps back into recording and review; theoretical consistency must not be used to suppress on-site material. [T-8]

Functions can genuinely recover in stages: when temporary teaching premises, transportation, teachers, and a term budget are available, educational functioning for this term can hold; an unreconstructed old school building does not make it false. If next month's rent or care lacks continuity, today's classes do not establish stability for the entire term. A later new shock does not retroactively negate earlier bounded achievements either; records should preserve the supporting conditions and closing window. [T-8]

The rules substantively cover normal accidents, near misses, drift, contraction, command, and recovery chains, but disaster types, hazard thresholds, statutory command, and professional cards must come from domain systems. Without on-site confirmation, a responsible professional, and valid emergency authorization, the framework provides only records and prompts, without delaying lifesaving action or replacing command. Page 35 of Maryland's 2023 ICS guide for a particular incident type separately lists unfinished recovery matters during transfer and closeout. It can illustrate distinct responsibilities, but is not a source of authorization for every disaster type. [T-8; P-ICS]

How the argument develops

  1. 1

    Specify this task's endpoint, window, object, and authority by stage and function.

  2. 2

    Recognize independent professional lifesaving duties; the framework must not cause delay.

  3. 3

    Preserve on-site dissent, inability to evacuate, and frontline signals.

  4. 4

    Separately check transfer, closeout, special-power durations, services, and recovery of everyday life.

  5. 5

    If on-site evidence overturns assumptions, step back into recording; acknowledge bounded achievements without declaring comprehensive recovery beyond the evidence.

Distinctions to keep clear

Successful rescue

Specified timely protection reaches its destination.

≠

Long-term recovery of everyday life

Services, burdens, relations, and rights require separate checks.

A partial-recovery combination

Some improvements coexist with unresolved gaps.

≠

Feedback trap

Requires a cross-period mechanism and competing explanations.

Command transfer

Command responsibility passes onward.

≠

Automatic termination or extension of powers

Check each item against its statutory duties and duration.

Bounded achievement

A function is genuinely available under supporting conditions.

≠

Claim of comprehensive recovery

Requires correspondingly broader evidence.

Teaching construction: two windows for a temporary schoolTeaching scenario

AssumptionsEntirely constructed scenarios and values, used to test inference ceilings.

A constructed emergency teaching arrangement has this month's premises, teachers' transportation, and budget, and classes actually operate normally this month; next month's rent has no funding source yet. The specified educational function may be recorded as recovered this month, but not as stable throughout the term. If a new shock later occurs, record the post-interruption state separately rather than erasing all of this month's real achievement.

BoundaryNot evidence from a real investigation, professional diagnosis, or effects of intervention.

Teaching construction: three different endpointsTeaching scenario

AssumptionsEntirely constructed scenarios and values, used to test inference ceilings.

A fictional record shows command handover completed on day A, one special power legally expiring on day B, and basic service continuity established on day C. A, B, and C are determined by different grounds. Handover does not establish recovery of residents' everyday lives, and their incomplete recovery does not automatically keep the power in B valid.

BoundaryNot evidence from a real investigation, professional diagnosis, or effects of intervention.

Scope and open questions

Check your understanding

  1. 1

    Must professional lifesaving action wait until the framework finishes its analysis?

  2. 2

    Does partial housing recovery establish a feedback trap?

  3. 3

    Can a temporary school that genuinely operates count as recovery?

  4. 4

    Does the departure of the coordinating body end every responsibility?

Must professional lifesaving action wait until the framework finishes its analysis?

No. The framework must not delay independent statutory and professional duties.

Basis: The EMG authority boundary.

Does partial housing recovery establish a feedback trap?

No. A partial-recovery combination does not itself establish a cross-period self-reinforcing mechanism.

Basis: EMG paragraph 2.

Can a temporary school that genuinely operates count as recovery?

It can hold within specified functions, periods, and supporting conditions; broader endpoints require separate checks.

Basis: The EMG teaching-scenario paragraph.

Does the departure of the coordinating body end every responsibility?

No. Unfinished matters, service continuity, power durations, and recovery of everyday life require separate checks.

Basis: EMG command continuity and ICS page 35.

15.3.9APP-ULS | Ultra-Large Scale ​

In briefAt ultra-large scales, objects, resources, and feedback across levels must be checked again; a wider range of impact does not expand authority to act, and local results cannot be copied directly into an overall prescription.
Codes used in this section (2)
  • T0Carriers of Safety and Trust
  • T4Exit, Transfer, and Preservation of Evolutionary Memory

The object is a nested system with boundaries, levels, jurisdiction, time window, key subsystems, resources/transmission/return flows, and external responses frozen. Register the whole, regions, groups, organizational levels, infrastructure, and external systems separately. Each move from local to aggregate, short-term to deep-time, or organizational to institutional requires reassessing object conversion, the nine-axis partial order, and K. An increase in scope of influence on the I axis does not expand authority to act on the J axis.

Major risks include using structural language to overestimate actual execution, insufficient resources and competing objectives, distortion of downstream transmission and feedback, obstruction by vested interests, reflexivity of metrics, fast risks crowding out slow variables, local failures spreading across levels, capture of governance, and large-scale irreversible side effects. A complete plan does not establish that resources are in place. Intentions at the center do not establish action at the downstream end. Short-term stability does not establish healthy slow variables.

Large-scale spatial and institutional options must also check whether aggregation mixes parcels, households, areas, and destinations into one denominator. Aggregate improvement can coincide with rising burdens on original residents, renters, people who moved out, or regions at the margins. Counts of new construction cannot be used to fill in relationships, memory, service eligibility, or actual choices. Preserve representation, minimum services, alternative arrangements to take over, and local options that can be rolled back for positions unable to exit or take another route.

Anomalous regions, minority groups, samples from the downstream end, nontextual experience, and absence signals must be brought back into the record through independent sampling. Disaggregate impacts by region, group, level, generation, and ability to exit. People unable to exit an institution, territory, or basic system receive representation, local exemptions, and minimum services. Changes in budgets, eligibility, employment, or services after submitting bad news enter anti-retaliation monitoring.

The module can produce only areas where judgment remains open, stress tests, trials at different levels, independent review, and candidates for T0–T4. It does not authorize a blanket prescription for the whole system or governance across domains. Stop expanding use and withdraw level by level if harm spreads across groups, resources and implementation capacity fall below the premises, metrics systematically conflict with field conditions, local appeals cannot be written back, or rollback capability is insufficient.

Scope of domain evidence and downgrading for gaps (substantial coverage). The rules cover blind spots, applicability switches, stress tests, and intervention priorities. Unified data, case registration, causal identification, representativeness, and methods of governance across domains still need to be established for the particular object. Without stratified samples, evidence of resource capacity, the execution chain, or evidence of rollback, do not extrapolate from the local to the aggregate, infer execution from intent, or propose a blanket option. Downgrade the output to areas where judgment remains open, a plan to obtain more evidence, and proposals for small-scale reversible trials.

15.3.9Note

Understanding this section

15.3.9 APP-ULS | Ultra-Large Scale

At ultra-large scales, objects, resources, and feedback across levels must be checked again; a wider range of impact does not expand authority to act, and local results cannot be copied directly into an overall prescription.

Brief quotation, translated from Chinese: “Expanding the range of impact on the I axis does not expand authority to act on the J axis.” Freeze the object's boundaries, levels, jurisdiction, window, critical subsystems, resource transmission and return flows, and external responses. Register the whole, regions, groups, organizational layers, infrastructure, and external systems separately. Moving from local to overall, short-term to deep time, or organization to institution requires rebuilding object conversion, the nine-axis partial order, and K. [T-9; T-scale]

Risks include structural language overstating execution, insufficient resources and competing objectives, distorted transmission and feedback at endpoints, obstruction by interests, indicator reflexivity, fast risks crowding out slow variables, local failures spreading across levels, capture, and irreversible side effects. A complete plan does not mean resources have arrived; central intention does not mean endpoint action; short-term stability does not mean healthy slow variables. Each of these three requires its own material; the same aggregate report cannot substitute for all of them. [T-9]

Large-scale spatial institutional proposals must avoid mixing denominators for plots, households, neighborhoods, and destinations. Aggregate improvements can coexist with increased burdens on original residents, renters, people who moved away, and peripheral regions; construction counts cannot fill gaps in relations, memory, service eligibility, and genuine choice. Preserve proxies, minimum services, alternative uptake, and reversible local options for those unable to exit or find another route. [T-9]

Anomalous regions, minority groups, endpoint samples, non-textual experience, and signals of absence should be independently sampled and reinserted, rather than accepting only material filtered by the center. Group impacts by region, population, level, generation, and ability to exit. Those unable to leave institutional, territorial, or basic systems need proxies, local exemptions, and minimum services. Changes in budgets, eligibility, careers, and services after bad-news reporting enter anti-retaliation monitoring. [T-9]

The output ceiling consists of undecided areas, stress tests, staged trials, independent review, and candidate T types; it grants neither a one-size-fits-all overall prescription nor cross-jurisdictional governance authority. When grouped harms spread, resource or execution capacity falls below premises, indicators systematically conflict with conditions on the ground, local appeals cannot write back, or rollback is inadequate, stop expansion and withdraw level by level. Withdrawal must also protect those already depending on pilot support; stopping must not be reduced to abruptly cutting off provision. [T-9; T-protection]

Substantive coverage locates rules for blind spots, switches, stress tests, and intervention priorities. Unified data, case registration, causal identification, representativeness, and cross-jurisdictional governance methods still need to be established for the object. Without evidence of stratified samples, capacity, execution chains, or rollback, do not infer the whole from the local or execution from intention. Downgrade to undecided areas, evidence-gathering plans, or recommendations for small reversible trials. Recommending a trial and actually starting it still differ in authority requirements. [T-9; T-main]

The original 2022 study by Egger and colleagues of regional cash transfers in Kenya explicitly states its external donor financing and single-region design, abstracting from nationwide monetary-policy and exchange-rate responses. Important, credible regional findings can exist without directly establishing nationwide policy effects. This does not mean nationwide implementation must fail or local findings are useless; it identifies conditions that must be added for a change of scale. [P-EGGER]

Ultra-large-scale analysis therefore must neither boast that “one model diagram solves nationwide problems” nor use complexity to reject all bounded judgments. Retaining verifiable local facts, specifying undecided areas, and designing proportionate independent validation and layered rollback make uncertainty specific to propositions and actions, rather than filling gaps with grand terminology. [T-9; T-main]

How the argument develops

  1. 1

    Distinguish nested objects; rebuild K and nine-axis relations across scales.

  2. 2

    Check resources, execution, and return flows at every level; central intention cannot replace endpoint facts.

  3. 3

    Preserve group-specific denominators, absences, and independent sampling.

  4. 4

    Bound the conditions for applying local findings to the whole and identify unknown external responses.

  5. 5

    Do not expand with insufficient evidence; stop and roll back level by level while maintaining valid protection.

Distinctions to keep clear

Large-sample regional trial

Can support the specified region and treatment.

≠

Nationwide policy

Financing, macro-level feedback, and execution conditions may differ.

Range of impact I

Where consequences may reach.

≠

Jurisdictional authority J

Cannot be inferred from widespread impact.

Central intention

Upstream plans and orders.

≠

Endpoint action

Requires chain and on-site evidence.

Aggregate improvement

A change in an aggregate measure.

≠

Benefits for every group

Requires tracking each group on a consistent basis.

Teaching construction: capacity does not multiply when replication increases tenfoldTeaching scenario

AssumptionsEntirely constructed scenarios and values, used to test inference ceilings.

In a constructed example, each of 10 pilot sites requires 2 specialists, totaling 20, while current total capacity is 30. Expanding directly to 100 sites requires 200, leaving a shortfall of 170. Success at the original pilots does not establish that execution premises for expansion hold. The calculation illustrates only resource constraints under the stated assumptions, not an estimate for any real project or professional staffing standard.

BoundaryNot evidence from a real investigation, professional diagnosis, or effects of intervention.

The boundary on nationwide extrapolation in the Kenyan regional transfer studyDocumented case

Page 2606 of the formally published 2022 paper by Egger and colleagues explicitly states that funding comes from outside the study area and that the regional design abstracts from nationwide monetary-policy and exchange-rate responses; page 2607 bounds the study location and period.

SourceEgger et al.: General Equilibrium Effects of Cash Transfers: Experimental Evidence From KenyaEconometrica 90(6), page 2606, second body paragraph; page 2607, §2.1Reading scope: Partly read

Scope and limitsThis is not a nationwide implementation experiment. It does not imply that nationwide implementation must fail or have small effects; it identifies only conditions missing when extrapolating from regional results.

Scope and open questions

Cases serve local factual or institutional comparisons; theoretical rules, original evidence, teaching constructions, and unresolved authority are labeled separately.

  • This lesson undertakes no execution in a real setting; professional protocols, field facts, valid authorization, and protective effects require separate verification.
  • External evidence supports only the propositions listed in the source table; material titles do not fill unread portions or unmeasured effects.

Do credible local trial results mean nationwide effects are known?

No. The object, financing, external responses, samples, and execution chain must be checked again.

Basis: ULS downgrading for missing material and Egger's local design.

Does affecting many regions confer cross-jurisdictional governance authority?

No. Expanding the I axis does not expand the J axis.

Basis: The first ULS paragraph.

What if overall indicators look good but local appeals cannot write back?

Aggregate results do not justify continued expansion; follow the source by stopping expansion and reviewing withdrawal level by level.

Basis: ULS stopping conditions.

15.4Minimum Output for an Application Record ​

In briefAn application record should let readers trace each judgment to its object, material, protection, and ceiling. A complete execution chain is added when entering real-world action; self-referential summaries cannot impersonate external responsible persons.
Codes used in this section (1)
  • C12Check on the Validity of Normative Bridging

Each application must retain at least the module ID, object, scale, K, and time window. It must record every supported proposition and its external evidence, coverage status and effects of gaps, material and tool inputs, domain risks, and affected, low-power, weak-signal, and unable-to-exit positions. It must include the protection floor, diagnosis and action ceiling, and how evidence gaps lower confidence and the level of judgment. Where a choice is needed, retain normative choice or a comparison with no action. Where intervention is needed, retain the candidate T level. Give reasons for inapplicable items. If proceeding to real-world action, attach the complete 17-field choice record wrapper, structured selected_action, C12, explicit N premises, O1–O4, the single atomic J authorization, stopping, anonymous appeals or appeals through a representative, anti-retaliation monitoring, rollback, and the execution state log.

In all module records, including those used only for diagnosis, references to evidence, positions, channels, and responsible parties must resolve to the runtime registry. When context is omitted, summary placeholders such as GHOST, none, self, or self:* must not substitute for external records. The parties responsible for appeal, independent review, and rollback must be distinct from the deciding subject.

An output missing these fields can serve only as a reading aid and cannot proceed to real-world action. An application proposed for real-world intervention must retain a bounded chain of action that can be changed by counterexamples, input from safe positions, and real-world consequences. A task limited to explanation or diagnosis ends at its corresponding evidential boundary.

15.4Note

Understanding this section

15.4 Minimum Output for Application Records

An application record should let readers trace each judgment to its object, material, protection, and ceiling. A complete execution chain is added when entering real-world action; self-referential summaries cannot impersonate external responsible persons.

Brief quotation, translated from Chinese: “Tasks that stop at explanation or diagnosis end at their corresponding evidentiary boundaries.” This section specifies a minimum traceable output without pushing every inquiry toward real-world intervention. Minimum does not mean the shorter the better; it means no necessary item determining “what may be said and what may be done” can be omitted. Completeness of an explanatory text and completeness of qualifications to execute are different responsibilities. [T-main]

The first group fixes identity and evidence: module ID; object, scale, K, and window; individually supported propositions, external evidence, coverage status, consequences of missing material, and material and tool inputs. Merely saying “the material is sufficient” is inadequate: identify which version supports which proposition and which inference each gap narrows. A domain name or an entire bibliography does not replace proposition-by-proposition support. [T-main; T-domain]

The second group fixes risks and protection: domain risks; affected, low-power, weak-signal, and unable-to-exit positions; the complete protection floor; diagnostic conclusions and action ceiling; and how evidence gaps lower confidence and level. Low-power positions cannot be treated as null values because they lack formal representatives or cannot express themselves fully. Even when weak signals have not become facts establishing responsibility, they still require protection pending verification. [T-main; T-protection]

The third group adds responsibilities according to use: where choice is needed, leave a normative-choice record or comparison with inaction; where intervention is needed, leave candidate T types; explain why any item is inapplicable. A text-only explanation may state that no option adoption is involved; an execution action must not be invented just to fill a form. Conversely, actually changing rights or resources cannot mark choice and authorization “not applicable.” Use is determined by actual consequences, not self-declared titles. [T-main; T-chain; T-strong]

Once real-world action begins, append the complete 17-field choice-record wrapper, structured selected_action, C12, explicit N, O1–O4, unique J atomic authorization, and provisions for stopping, anonymous/proxy appeals, anti-retaliation monitoring, rollback, and an execution-state log. This paragraph requires a complete record consistent with the corresponding engineering contract; this explanation neither reworks its semicolon-separated list into an invented “17 fields” nor certifies that particular software implements it. Actual implementations must check fields and semantics against their frozen versions, not rely solely on field counts. [T-main; T-permission; T-types]

In all records, including diagnosis-only records, references to evidence, positions, channels, and responsible persons must resolve to the runtime registry. Resolution requires more than a string's existence: it must reach the specific referenced object, source, and responsibility position. When context is omitted, GHOST, none, self, or self:* summaries cannot replace external records; those responsible for appeals, independent review, and rollback cannot be the decision-making actor. Changing aliases while retaining the same actual controller does not achieve the required separation. [T-main]

Resolvable references do not establish that their contents are true, that responsible persons are effectively independent, that channels are reachable, or that a decision is legally valid; they merely make further checks possible. Diagnosis also requires resolution: not executing yet does not exempt material and affected positions from traceability responsibilities. Conversely, complete diagnostic references do not confer execution authority. [T-main; T-domain; T-permission]

Module outputs missing these necessary fields can only be reading prompts and cannot enter real-world action. Proposed action requires a bounded action chain that counterexamples, safety positions, and real consequences can change, rather than repackaging the original conclusion to make it harder to refute. Stopping, correcting records, downstream write-back, and actual remedy require separate checks; a file displaying completed does not independently establish recovery for harmed positions. [T-main; T-state]

This section specifies records; this discussion does not treat an institution's “having a ledger” as a success case. The teaching examples below concretely test boundaries involving references, use, and state. They generate no actual permission, real personnel list, or executable action record, and do not disguise this research package as the registry of a real-world task. [T-main]

How the argument develops

  1. 1

    First fix whether this output ends at explanation, diagnosis, choice, or execution.

  2. 2

    Leave an object, source, scope, and gaps for each conclusion.

  3. 3

    Register protected positions and ceilings; inapplicability requires proportionate reasons.

  4. 4

    Resolve all references to external runtime records; separate key review roles from the decision-making actor.

  5. 5

    Append a complete choice-and-execution contract only when entering action; missing necessary items prohibit action.

  6. 6

    Let counterexamples and consequences genuinely change states; check correction effects beyond traceability.

Distinctions to keep clear

Minimum output

Necessary responsibilities cannot be omitted; configure them by task.

≠

Shortest summary

May erase crucial scope and gaps.

Successful resolution

A reference reaches a specific registry entry.

≠

Facts/authority established

Content, independence, and validity still require checking.

Endpoint of an explanatory task

A grounded explanation of the question may conclude the task.

≠

Real-world intervention

Requires the complete choice–authorization–execution chain.

Different role labels

Names or accounts differ.

≠

Different responsible parties

Actual identities and control relationships must be checked.

Teaching construction: different gaps in three referencesTeaching scenario

AssumptionsIDs and scenario are artificial, with no actual identities or external action.

A fictional record references evidence E1, appeal channel C1, and reviewer R1. E1 reaches a versioned material; C1 is merely a line saying ‘contact the responsible party’, with no actual entry point; R1 resolves to the decision-maker. E1's resolvability does not fill the latter two gaps. The current output may retain textual analysis within E1's support scope, but cannot thereby enter actual action requiring effective appeals and independent review.

BoundaryResolvability and independence are different checks; creating another ID alone does not pass.

Teaching construction: an explanation need not end with an interventionTeaching scenario

AssumptionsA fictional task transition.

An artificial task asks only for the meaning of a public rule. After recording the material version, object, conclusion, and uncertainties, it may end at the explanatory boundary; normative choice, candidate execution plans, and similar items are marked not applicable with reasons. A later request to change user qualifications changes the task and consequences, requiring renewed checks of choice, protection, and authorization rather than directly upgrading the explanatory record into an execution record.

BoundaryPure explanation need not fabricate an actual execution contract; changed use cannot claim exemption from an old record.

15.5Starting Dynamic Analysis in the Application Modules ​

In briefEnable dynamic analysis according to the question, first specifying agents, circles, conditions, clocks, and event status. Simulations remain simulations; complex procedures add no actual authority.

When dynamic analysis is needed, all nine application modules must additionally declare the main actor, primary circle, neighboring circles, relation types, M/Ψ conditions, five kinds of clock, event, simple baseline, and outcome write-back. The relationship and family modules focus on role activation, inability to exit, and slow, intermediate-timescale, and fast states. The organization and platform modules focus on metrics, bridging, propagation, and institutional write-back. The public governance, public opinion, and ultra-large-scale modules focus on representation, positions with low visibility, losses in aggregation across levels, and calibration drift. The space and emergency modules focus on material channels, capacity, thresholds, delay, and emergency authorization.

No module may bypass an event’s factual status because “the situation is urgent,” or bypass privacy and protection of people affected because “the model is only making a suggestion.” An emergency permits only minimum protective action under external emergency rules, with review, appeal, and rollback restored as soon as possible. Scenarios generated by the model retain hypothetical or simulated status and must not be written back as observed.

If an application only needs explanation, do not require multi-circle foresight. If a simple baseline is already sufficient, retain a simpler module record. If foresight lacks registration or calibration, the output stops at path prompts. If authorization is incomplete, stop real-world execution and retain requirements for action, analytical recommendations that confer no execution permission, and drafts of institutions and plans. The existence of a complex workflow must not create pressure to take real-world action.

15.5Note

Understanding this section

15.5 Dynamic entry into application modules

Enable dynamic analysis according to the question, first specifying agents, circles, conditions, clocks, and event status. Simulations remain simulations; complex procedures add no actual authority.

Short quotation: ‘the existence of a complex process cannot become pressure for actual action upon an object’ (translated from Chinese). The nine modules add dynamic entry records only when dynamic analysis is needed. Dynamics does not upgrade every matter into multi-circle prediction; when a question involves change, cross-level transmission, or delay, it makes update grounds explicit. Explanation alone does not force foresight, and sufficient simple baselines permit simple records. [T-main]

Required additions are the main agent, main circle, adjacent circles, relationship types, M/Ψ conditions, five clocks, events, a simple baseline, and result write-back. M denotes material conditions and Ψ experience–meaning conditions; both need observational or interpretive grounds. Subjective experience cannot be read directly from external resource quantities, nor experiential narratives automatically converted into a complete account of external facts. [T-main；T-MP]

The five clocks are immediate, interactional, organizational, institutional, and long-term. Immediate attention may change with signals; interactional trust takes rounds; organizational budgets follow decision/execution cycles; institutional change concerns rules and actual write-back; long-term capability depends on accumulated maintenance. Time units are typical examples, not fixed minutes or years for a variable. An event directly updates only variables reached through channels with conditions satisfied; unreached does not mean eternally unchanged in reality. [T-clock]

Four domain emphases must not be flattened together: relationships/households examine role activation, inability to exit, and slow/intermediate/fast states; organizations/platforms examine metrics, bridging, transmission, and institutional write-back; public governance/public discourse/very large scale examine representation, low-visibility positions, cross-level aggregation losses, and calibration drift; spatial/emergency tasks examine material channels, capacity thresholds and delays, and emergency authorization. Each emphasis is an entry to questions, not a mechanism established before evidence. [T-main]

Events must retain factual status. Model-generated scenarios are hypothetical or simulated and cannot be written back as observed; an actual historical starting point also does not turn synthetic subsequent trajectories into occurred facts. Result write-back should distinguish observation, prediction, and error; predictions cannot be entered into training data/files and then counted as external validation. [T-main；T-event]

‘The situation is urgent’ cannot bypass event factual status, and ‘only a recommendation’ does not exempt privacy and affected-person protection. Emergency actions use only external emergency rules for minimal protection, restoring review, appeals, and rollback promptly; the framework creates no emergency powers. Existing professional life-saving duties must not be delayed by structural analysis, while the model cannot use them to take over the scene. [T-main；T-emergency]

When foresight is unregistered or uncalibrated, output stops at path indications. Calibration is not making one story sound plausible, but a checkable comparison of corresponding predictions and later outcomes under conditions and windows. A simple baseline shows whether complexity is worth using; if a simple approach sufficiently answers the current question, unverifiable parameters need not be added for procedural completeness. [T-main；T-forecast]

Incomplete authorization stops actual execution while permitting action needs, analytical recommendations that create no execution authority, and draft institutional plans to remain. Analysis may have an explicit preferred option, but cannot package it as an approved command or pressure agents with ‘the whole process ran, so not executing would waste it’. Actions supported by independently valid professional duties in prior materials follow their own scope, not authority borrowed from model recommendations. [T-main；T-permission]

Mansoury and colleagues' 2020 paper explicitly defines ‘time’ as successive offline interaction iterations rather than calendar time and generates subsequent responses in simulation. This concrete design distinguishes model clocks from real events: actual initial data and synthetic continuation may coexist, but round 20 cannot be called an actual user's day 20. This lesson neither reproduces the computations nor uses the paper to establish this framework's predictive capability. [P-MANS]

How the argument develops

  1. 1

    First ask whether dynamic or multi-circle foresight is actually needed.

  2. 2

    If needed, fix agent/circle identities, relationships, M/Ψ, five clocks, and event grounds.

  3. 3

    Retain a simple baseline and specify the most important domain risks and protections.

  4. 4

    Separate observations, hypotheses, and simulations; result write-back must not turn them into facts.

  5. 5

    Unregistered/uncalibrated foresight is reduced to path indications; incomplete authority stops execution.

  6. 6

    Retain grounded analysis and conditional recommendations without pressuring action through procedural complexity.

Distinctions to keep clear

Model iteration

Advance one round under model rules.

≠

Calendar time

Requires a corresponding real-time mapping.

Actual starting point

Initial data come from observation.

≠

Actual continuation

Synthetic updates remain simulations.

Path indication

Suggests possible developments.

≠

Calibrated prediction

Requires corresponding registration, comparison, and testing.

Analytical recommendation

Reasons and a preferred option for deliberation.

≠

Permission to execute

Comes from valid choice and independent authority.

Teaching construction: two clocks cannot be forced into synchronyTeaching scenario

AssumptionsDates, procedures, and organization are fictional, illustrating asynchronous responsibilities only.

An artificial organization receives a service alert today, so immediate risk records may update; a budget adjustment still requires next week's meeting and has not been implemented. Today's alert therefore cannot also be recorded as ‘budget reallocated’. If backend operations provide necessary support in advance under an established independent procedure, record its grounds and actions separately rather than inferring a budget resolution from a risk record.

BoundaryActual organizations are not required to wait for meetings; emergency duties and valid independent authority require separate checks.

Teaching construction: an observed value and two continuationsTeaching scenario

Assumptions10, 8, 6, and 7 are teaching values; absolute errors |8−7|=1 and |6−7|=1.

The artificial starting observation is inventory 10; model A predicts 8 next round and model B predicts 6. Only starting value 10 is observed within the stipulation; both continuations are simulated. Only after later actual verification gives 7 may a new observation be added and errors compared as 1 and 1. One cannot first enter 8 into a file and then use that file to ‘confirm’ model A.

BoundaryIdentical one-round errors establish neither equal overall calibration nor authority over inventory.

Teaching construction: static explanation sufficesTeaching scenario

AssumptionsArtificial task selection.

A fictional task asks only what ‘expires on the due date’ means in a public rule. If the source and period information suffice, no ten-year forecast of adjacent circles is needed. Only a later question about intertemporal effects of exit arrangements on different dependents calls for clocks, events, baselines, and protections under the new task; the earlier simple task was not incomplete.

BoundaryA simple method must still satisfy the task's actual evidential and protective responsibilities.

Time in offline recommendation simulation is not calendar timeDocumented case

The final paragraph of §1 and §2 in Mansoury and colleagues' 2020 paper describe offline simulation with time expressed as successive interaction iterations; simulated continuation cannot masquerade as events real users experienced through calendar time.
